## 10. Wave-20 loop repairs (DX5)

Commission: Charlie Cheever's wave-20 fix list #4, #6, #7, #8;
implementer Codex, 2026-10-21. This amendment is proposed until its two
independent reviews and implementation evidence are recorded. SEC5 owns
security intent, campaigns and exposure output; this lane changes lookup
advice, never the authority granted by an application rule.

### Clock reports

Amend LLP 3000.000.000.002 §4's proof helper return: `advance(duration)`
returns `{now, fired, held}`. Each entry carries the schedule name, target,
reason, boundary/window metadata and bounded run summary from the existing
operator-only schedule report. `now()` still returns a number. The CLI and
HTTP advance reply expose the same arrays, retaining `schedules` for existing
operator consumers. Fired means a schedule was enqueued, not that its job
succeeded; the run summary distinguishes parked or pending work. Every
non-fired schedule appears in held with a reason, including an already
processed boundary, a future saved boundary, initialization, a future window
or an explicit hold. Saved boundaries survive restart: one fire per boundary,
coalescing missed periods unless eachBoundary was explicitly requested.
The helper and CLI print saved-boundary holds and their recovery action on
stderr, including the equal-boundary case on a reused store. Advance never
rewinds markers or replays a completed boundary. Reply limits account for the
retained report plus its partition into fired/held. Staging's expiry notice
describes expiry/upload recovery without development-door instructions.
Ambiguous or failed advances are never retried; time may already have moved.
Maintenance failures return an explicitly incomplete schedule report with the
advanced time; the proof helper attaches this reply to its thrown error.

### Source diagnostics without an existence oracle

Extend LLP 3000.036.002 §15.2's N_LOOKUP_FILTERED advice to required reads
and reads of written tables. A later write and an asserted `! else CODE` do
not prove read authority. Existing key/flow proofs still suppress advice,
including prior successful exact reads and deliberately public projections.
One note names the source lookup, authored hiding rule, declaration and the
null/custom-refusal consequence; duplicate N_LOOKUP_HIDDEN notes at that
site are avoided (the more specific N_LOOKUP_HIDDEN takes precedence). This is missing-proof advice, not a claim every caller
is refused. Program `exists` and rule-witness `exists` keep distinct semantics.

For private tables with secondary unique keys, source advice explains that
an unreadable conflicting row uses generic E_RULE (or an undisclosed write
target miss), even when the unique declaration has `else CODE`. The named
constraint applies only when the conflict can be disclosed. Do not return
the declared code only on hidden conflicts: that would violate LLP 3000 §7
and LLP 3000.036.002 §15.2. Public E_RULE repair text, if changed, is identical
for ordinary rule rejection and hidden collision. No row, key, actual hiding
clause or hidden-dependent meter enters the public refusal. Rewrites propose
a minimal readable key projection or operator-mediated ownership/claim flow,
never broader disclosure of private rows. Paired hidden/missing lookup tests assert equality of public diagnostics and
logical meters. Hidden/ordinary write-refusal tests compare public refusals
and receipts; write replies expose no meter.

### Upgrade advice reaches the old CLI

Extend §8's bounded scan with candidate `data ... --json` consumers in authored
scripts, including argv-array and shell forms. List paths without printing
source. State the one-line migration `JSON.parse(stdout).rows` for the former
bare array, and preserve `more`/`limit`. This is a candidate scan, not an AST
proof or an automatic rewrite; report scan limits.

The installed wrapper runs project warnings before the first ordinary check
for that installed version, independently of the runtime-history receipt.
A warning receipt is written only after delivery to a terminal (or an empty
scan). Piped/captured stderr cannot establish delivery: old quiet upgrades
discard it, so a nonempty scan stays unacknowledged and the next ordinary
check repeats the advice, including in CI. Baseline checks neither deliver
nor acknowledge warnings; read/receipt failures do not fail compilation.
Warnings always use stderr, preserving one-object JSON stdout and quiet-mode
visibility. This reaches the usual published 0.4.33/0.4.35 upgrade path because
their upgrade invokes the newly installed wrapper for check. A fresh-process
resolution must select new bytes after package replacement. Direct upgrade
keeps its existing pre-install warning behavior. Test both published old CLIs
against the fresh packed package in an isolated local registry, including
--quiet and --json --quiet and the deferred first check; do not claim
an upgrade was tested by invoking only the new helper.

### Frontend and starter custody

Extend LLP 3000.013.002 §2 with `ReadState` in snapback4/react: a list read
(or PageHook) renders loading, denied, empty, or authorized data through one
component. It adds no subscription, cache or authority. It preserves partial
and stale rows; empty means the returned list is empty, never proven absence.
Loading and empty default to null; denied uses the supplied renderer or
throws the existing QueryRefusal for an error boundary. Children receive the
typed list and precise settled read metadata. Browser and React Native
callers supply their own display elements.

The Expo adapter owns `snapback4-expo/metro` (CommonJS withSnapback(config))
and its wasm transformer. Resolve Expo's transformer relative to the consuming
project/config, compatible with isolated package-manager installs. Preserve
the caller's config and append the existing .snapback4 block and wasm support.
New starter Metro config only obtains Expo's default and calls withSnapback.
The adapter also owns the native smoke sign-in hook; new starters import it
instead of carrying src/native-smoke.ts. Password and guest selection remain
explicit; ordinary launches never sign in automatically. Old modified helpers
remain app-owned. No native engine or simulator custody changes.

Amend LLP 3000.011.003.000 §7.2: adapt replaces an untouched todo frontend
proof with a runnable proof scaffold retaining frontend:proof/proof:web and
Playwright. It starts the correct frontend and checks rendered content, then
explicitly refuses to claim an app-specific write proof until the builder
adds one. A custom proof is never rewritten. Fresh non-todo starters get the
same scaffold. Every Expo starter includes playwright-core, including custom
schemas. Qualification runs changed guide/starter sources from the packed
tarball, tests the expected scaffold refusal, and records frontend character
reductions on copies of three wave-20 Expo lanes. No original lane is edited.

### Acceptance and scope

Full five-crate Rust tests, affected client tests, fresh-pack Linux consumer
qualification with per-item cases and published-old-CLI upgrades, Mac Studio
affected platform tests, ref-check, docs budget and repository-root checks.
No test.sh, publication, push or version bump is authorized by this work.
WORKSTREAM-REPORT.md records exact commands/results, commits and limitations;
review transcripts and source provenance live in llp/reviews/dx5/.

exports.withSnapback = function (config) {

    ...config,

      ...config.resolver,

      assetExts: [...new Set([...(config.resolver?.assetExts ?? []), "wasm"])],
    },
    transformer: { ...config.transformer, babelTransformerPath: require.resolve("./metro-wasm-transformer.cjs") },

};
// Metro resolves the consumer's Expo toolchain, including isolated installs.
const { createRequire } = require("node:module");
const { join } = require("node:path");
exports.transform = function (args) {
  const requireApp = createRequire(join(args.options.projectRoot, "package.json"));
  const expoRequire = createRequire(requireApp.resolve("expo/metro-config"));
  const upstream = expoRequire("@expo/metro-config/babel-transformer");
  const src = args.options.platform === "web"
    ? args.src.replace(/new URL\(("\.\/wasm\/snapback4_device_bg\.wasm"), import\.meta\.url\)/g, "require($1)")
    : args.src;
  return upstream.transform({ ...args, src });
};
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#10-wave-20-loop-repairs-dx5 — sign-in is confined to the owned native prime launch.
import { useEffect, useRef } from "react";
import { useAuth } from "snapback4/react";
import { smokeAccount, smokeSegment } from "./witness";

/** Ordinary launches do nothing. Password apps explicitly opt into the
 * driver's disposable account; guest apps keep ordinary guest sign-in. */
export function useNativeSmoke(password = false) {
  const auth = useAuth(), attempted = useRef(false);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (smokeSegment() !== "prime" || auth.state !== "signed-out" || attempted.current) return;
    const account = password ? smokeAccount() : null;
    if (password && !account) return;
    attempted.current = true;
    if (account) void auth.signup(account.email, account.password);
    else void auth.guest();
  }, [auth, password]);
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#8-wave-18-developer-loop-amendment-dx4 — bounded candidate scan, never an automatic script rewrite.
// Project-specific migration advice. Read authored files only; never print their contents.
import { readdirSync, readFileSync, lstatSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, writeFileSync, renameSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, dirname } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
const excluded = new Set(['node_modules', '.git', '.snapback4', 'generated', 'dist', 'build', 'target', 'deploy', 'logs', 'store', 'output', '.runtime']);
export function upgradeWarnings(root, declarations) {
  const doors = [], persistence = [], dataJson = [];
  let scanned = 0, incomplete = false;
  const walk = (dir, prefix = '', depth = 0) => {
    if (scanned > 10000 || depth > 8) { incomplete = true; return; }
    let entries;
    try { entries = readdirSync(dir, {withFileTypes: true}); } catch { incomplete = true; return; }
    for (const entry of entries.sort((a,b)=>a.name.localeCompare(b.name))) {
      if (++scanned > 10000) { incomplete = true; return; }
      if (excluded.has(entry.name) || entry.name.startsWith('.')) continue;
      const relative = prefix + entry.name, path = join(dir, entry.name);
      if (entry.isDirectory()) { walk(path, relative + '/', depth + 1); continue; }
      if (!entry.isFile() || !/\.(?:[cm]?[jt]sx?|sh|json)$/.test(entry.name)) continue;
      let size; try { size = lstatSync(path).size; } catch { incomplete = true; continue; }
      if (size > 1048576) { incomplete = true; continue; }
      let source; try { source = readFileSync(path, 'utf8'); } catch { incomplete = true; continue; }
      if (/\/seed\b|\/dev\/|x-snapback-persona/.test(source)) doors.push(relative);
      if (/\bstartDev\s*\(/.test(source)) persistence.push(relative);
      // Candidate scan: shell commands, argv arrays and npm-script strings.
      // Never infer how the parsed result is used or rewrite application code.
      if (/\bdata\b[^\n]{0,2000}--json/.test(source) || /--json[^\n]{0,2000}\bdata\b/.test(source)) dataJson.push(relative);
    }
  };
  walk(root);
  const warnings = [];
  const passwordOnly = /^\s*use[ \t]+identity[ \t]+password\b/m.test(declarations) && !/^\s*use[ \t]+identity(?:[ \t]*(?:--[^\n]*)?)?$/m.test(declarations);
  if (passwordOnly) warnings.push('password-only dev doors are CLOSED since 0.4.33: /seed, /dev/* and persona headers refuse. Use deploy staging --staging plus serve staging for real users (guide staging); local fixtures explicitly opt into dev --unsafe-dev-doors.' + (doors.length ? ' Review: ' + doors.join(', ') : ' No matching dev-door scripts found.'));
  if (persistence.length) warnings.push('startDev() persists since 0.4.33: reruns see old rows and share the dev store. For disposable acceptance use startDev({args:["--memory"]}); keep persistence for continuity. Review (check each call for explicit memory): ' + persistence.join(', '));
  if (dataJson.length) warnings.push('data --json returns {rows, more, limit} since 0.4.35, replacing the bare array. One-line fix: JSON.parse(stdout).rows (was JSON.parse(stdout)); use more/limit to detect truncation. Review candidate consumers: ' + dataJson.join(', '));
  if (incomplete) warnings.push('migration scan incomplete (unreadable/large files or depth/file limit); inspect remaining authored scripts for /seed, /dev/*, persona headers, startDev() and data --json array consumers.');
  return warnings;
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#10-wave-20-loop-repairs-dx5 — the OLD CLI invokes the NEW wrapper for its post-upgrade check.
export function firstCheckWarnings(cwd = process.cwd()) {
  if (process.env.SNAPBACK4_UPGRADE_BASELINE === '1') return;
  let temporary;
  try {
    let root = cwd;
    while (!existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) { const parent = dirname(root); if (parent === root) return; root = parent; }
    const schema = join(root, 'snapback');
    if (!existsSync(schema)) return;
    const version = JSON.parse(readFileSync(fileURLToPath(new URL('../package.json', import.meta.url)), 'utf8')).version;
    const receipt = join(root, '.snapback4/project-warnings-version.json');
    try { if (JSON.parse(readFileSync(receipt, 'utf8')).version === version) return; } catch { /* First check or unreadable receipt: deliver. */ }
    const declarations = readdirSync(schema).filter(name => name.endsWith('.q')).map(name => readFileSync(join(schema, name), 'utf8')).join('\n');
    const warnings = upgradeWarnings(root, declarations);
    const name = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8')).name ?? root;
    for (const warning of warnings) process.stderr.write(`project ${name}: upgrade warning: ${warning}\n`);
    // Old upgrade --quiet captures and discards check stderr. A pipe is not
    // evidence of delivery: leave advice pending for the next visible check.
    if (warnings.length && !process.stderr.isTTY) return;
    mkdirSync(dirname(receipt), {recursive:true});
    temporary = `${receipt}.${randomUUID()}.tmp`;
    writeFileSync(temporary, JSON.stringify({version}) + '\n', {flag:'wx'});
    renameSync(temporary, receipt);
  } catch {
    process.stderr.write('snapback4: project migration advice unavailable or not acknowledged; check will continue. Review guide changes and run upgrade to scan authored scripts.\n');
  } finally { if (temporary) try { rmSync(temporary, {force:true}); } catch { /* Advisory only. */ } }
}
#!/usr/bin/env node
// `npx snapback4 <verb>`: the Rust binary, found in the platform package
// installed beside this one, or named by SNAPBACK4_BIN, or built in this
// repository. The JavaScript here only finds and runs it, and the two live and
// die together: SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP to this wrapper are forwarded, and
// SIGKILL, which cannot be forwarded, still stops the binary: it is told this
// wrapper's PID (SNAPBACK4_SUPERVISOR_PID) and exits when its parent is gone
// (Linux: the kernel's parent-death signal; elsewhere within 250 ms). So a
// recorded PID of either stops the server; `GET /dev/status` reports both
// (`pid` is the binary, `wrapperPid` this wrapper), and so does the stderr line
// `SNAPBACK4_READY … url=… pid=… wrapperPid=…`.
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
import { resolveBinary } from "../dist/resolve-binary.js";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { constants } from "node:os";
import { firstCheckWarnings } from "./upgrade-warnings.js";

if (process.argv[2] === "check" && !process.argv.includes("--help")) firstCheckWarnings();

if (process.argv[2] === "web-shell") {
  try { await (await import("./web-shell.js")).runWebShell(process.argv.slice(3)); }
  catch (error) { console.error(`E_INPUT at web-shell: ${error.message}\n  rewrite: export a static app, then run snapback4 web-shell dist --base /`); process.exit(2); }
  process.exit(0);
}

let binary;
try { binary = resolveBinary(); }
catch (error) { console.error(error.message); process.exit(2); }
// Internal export helpers share the wrapper's kernel lease through fd 3.
const exportLease = process.argv[2] === "witness" && ["export-lease", "export-publish"].includes(process.argv[3]);
const child = spawn(binary, process.argv.slice(2), { stdio: exportLease ? ["inherit", "inherit", "inherit", 3] : "inherit", env: {
  ...process.env, SNAPBACK4_ACQUIRE_HELPER: fileURLToPath(new URL("./witness-acquire.js", import.meta.url)),
  SNAPBACK4_UPGRADE_HELPER: fileURLToPath(new URL("./upgrade.js", import.meta.url)),
  SNAPBACK4_WEB_HELPER: fileURLToPath(new URL("./witness-web.js", import.meta.url)),
  SNAPBACK4_SUPERVISOR_PID: String(process.pid),
} });
const handlers = new Map(["SIGINT", "SIGTERM", "SIGHUP"].map(signal => [signal, () => { try { child.kill(signal); } catch { /* gone */ } }]));
for (const [signal, handler] of handlers) process.on(signal, handler);
// `npx snapback4 dev` puts npm and `sh -c` above this wrapper. A SIGTERM to the
// npx PID kills npm and the shell but never reaches us, so the server would keep
// serving as an orphan. Our parent's death is the stop signal. (`process.ppid` is
// read once at startup, so probe the original parent instead.)
const parent = process.ppid;
const parentAlive = () => { try { process.kill(parent, 0); return true; } catch (error) { return error.code === "EPERM"; } };
const orphanWatch = parent > 1 ? setInterval(() => {
  if (!parentAlive()) { try { child.kill("SIGTERM"); } catch { /* gone */ } }
}, 250) : null;
orphanWatch?.unref();
child.on("exit", (code, signal) => {
  if (orphanWatch) clearInterval(orphanWatch);
  for (const [name, handler] of handlers) process.off(name, handler);
  if (signal) {
    // Restore the default disposition before re-raising. Some platforms do not
    // terminate on this call; never let their empty event loop report success.
    const status = 128 + (constants.signals[signal] ?? { SIGHUP: 1, SIGINT: 2, SIGTERM: 15 }[signal] ?? 1);
    setTimeout(() => process.exit(status), 100);
    try { process.kill(process.pid, signal); } catch { process.exit(status); }
    return;
  }
  process.exit(code ?? 1);
});

//! A process-local clock for development and explicitly classified staging stores.
use snapback4_core::error::Refusal;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#8-wave-18-developer-loop-amendment-dx4 — preserve expiry tests and tell callers how to recover.
pub(crate) const SESSION_NOTICE: &str = "Time travel also advances session expiry and unplaced-upload collection: seven-day password sessions may now be expired. Sign in again after the jump and upload unplaced bytes after it; never replay an ambiguous clock advance.";

const MAX_TIME: i64 = snapback4_core::value::I53_MAX;

pub fn input(message: impl Into<String>) -> Refusal { Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_INPUT", "clock", message).guide("clock") }
pub fn release() -> Refusal { Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_DEV_ONLY", "clock", "clock controls require dev or a deploy --staging store; production always uses wall time").guide("clock") }

/// Isolated time tests stay inside an assigned range, or request a free port.
pub(crate) fn isolated_command() -> String {
    isolated_range(std::env::var("PORT_LO").ok().as_deref(), std::env::var("PORT_HI").ok().as_deref())
}
fn isolated_range(lo: Option<&str>, hi: Option<&str>) -> String {
    match (lo.and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok()), hi.and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok())) {
        (Some(lo), Some(hi)) if lo > 0 && hi >= lo => format!("dev --memory --port {lo}-{hi} within the current range"),
        _ => "dev --memory --port 0".into(),
    }
}

pub fn duration(text: &str) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    if text.starts_with('-') { return Err(input("clock advance cannot move backwards; use a positive duration such as +2m")); }
    let text = text.strip_prefix('+').unwrap_or(text);
    let split = text.bytes().position(|b| !b.is_ascii_digit()).unwrap_or(text.len());
    let (number, unit) = text.split_at(split);
    let multiplier = match unit { "ms" => 1, "s" => 1_000, "m" => 60_000, "h" => 3_600_000, "d" => 86_400_000, "w" => 604_800_000, _ => 0 };
    number.parse::<i64>().ok().and_then(|n| n.checked_mul(multiplier)).filter(|n| *n > 0 && *n <= MAX_TIME)
        .ok_or_else(|| input("expected a positive whole duration with ms, s, m, h, d or w, such as +25h"))
}

pub fn offset(text: &str) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    if let Some(rest) = text.strip_prefix('-') { duration(rest).map(|n| -n) } else { duration(text) }
}

fn time(value: Option<i64>) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    value.filter(|n| (0..=MAX_TIME).contains(n)).ok_or_else(|| input("time must be Unix milliseconds in 0..9007199254740991; choose a smaller time or duration"))
}

pub fn run_now(text: Option<&String>) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    let now = snapback4_core::now_ms();
    match text {
        None => Ok(now),
        Some(text) if text.starts_with('+') => time(now.checked_add(duration(text)?)),
        Some(text) => time(text.parse().ok()),
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Clock {
    dev: bool,
    base: i64,
    offset: i64,
    started: Instant,
    epoch: String,
    revision: u64,
    #[cfg(test)]
    frozen: bool,
}

impl Clock {
    pub fn new(dev: bool, offset: i64) -> Result<Self, Refusal> {
        if !dev && offset != 0 { return Err(release()); }
        Ok(Self { dev, offset, base: time(snapback4_core::now_ms().checked_add(offset))?, started: Instant::now(),
            epoch: snapback4_core::ids::mint(snapback4_core::now_ms(), &mut snapback4_core::ids::Mint::default()).map_err(|e| e.refusal())?, revision: 0, #[cfg(test)] frozen: false })
    }
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(crate) fn freeze(&mut self, now: i64) { self.base = now; self.frozen = true; }
    pub fn now(&self) -> i64 {
        #[cfg(test)] if self.frozen { return self.base; }
        if !self.dev { return snapback4_core::now_ms(); }
        self.base.saturating_add(self.started.elapsed().as_millis().min(MAX_TIME as u128) as i64).min(MAX_TIME)
    }
    /// Identifies samples taken before/after a restart or deliberate clock jump.
    pub fn offset(&self) -> i64 { self.offset }
    pub fn revision(&self) -> String { format!("{}:{}", self.epoch, self.revision) }
    pub fn presence_now(&self) -> i64 {
        // Production grace is elapsed real time, unaffected by wall-clock corrections.
        if self.dev { self.now() } else { self.started.elapsed().as_millis().min(MAX_TIME as u128) as i64 }
    }
    /// Back to wall time: the offset `--clock-offset` and every advance added
    /// is dropped (a development reset's `{"clock":"reset"}`).
    pub fn reset(&mut self) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
        if !self.dev { return Err(release()); }
        self.revision += 1;
        self.offset = 0;
        self.base = snapback4_core::now_ms();
        self.started = Instant::now();
        #[cfg(test)] { self.frozen = false; }
        Ok(self.base)
    }
    pub fn advance(&mut self, milliseconds: i64) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
        if !self.dev { return Err(release()); }
        if milliseconds <= 0 { return Err(input("clock advance cannot move backwards; use a positive duration such as +2m")); }
        let next = time(self.now().checked_add(milliseconds))?;
        let offset = self.offset.checked_add(milliseconds).ok_or_else(|| input("cumulative clock offset overflow"))?;
        self.revision += 1;
        self.offset = offset;
        self.base = next;
        self.started = Instant::now();
        Ok(next)
    }
}

/// The control CLI only talks to a loopback dev host. It does not open its store.
pub fn command(options: &crate::verbs::Options) -> i32 {
    let result = (|| -> Result<String, String> {
        if options.positionals.len() != 2 || options.positionals[0] != "advance" {
            return Err(input(format!("usage: {}", crate::cli_flags::synopsis("clock"))).to_string());
        }
        duration(&options.positionals[1]).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let release_path = options.flags.get("release").map(|dir| std::path::PathBuf::from(dir).join("store.sqlite"));
        if release_path.is_some() && options.flags.contains_key("port") { return Err("clock --release does not accept --port".into()); }
        let (address, instance, token) = if let Some(path) = &release_path {
            let store = snapback4_core::Store::open_read_only(path).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
            if store.meta("deployment_environment").map_err(|e|e.to_string())?.as_deref() != Some("staging") { return Err(release().to_string()); }
            let address = crate::store_owner::inspector_address(path).ok_or("staging clock requires a running serve")?;
            let session = crate::serve::token::mint_live(path, "clock", 1).map_err(|(_,error)|error)?;
            (address,None,Some(session.token))
        } else { let (address,instance)=crate::verbs::dev_address(options)?; (address,instance,None) };
        let body = serde_json::json!({"duration":options.positionals[1],"eachBoundary":options.flags.contains_key("each-boundary")}).to_string();
        // The common HTTP/1.0 exchange is EOF-delimited and bounds replies at
        // 64 MiB, enough for the preflight's complete explicit window report.
        let response = if let Some(token) = &token {
            crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange_authorized(address,"POST","/dev/clock/advance",None,Some(token),&body,Duration::from_secs(60))
        } else { crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange_dev(address, "/dev/clock/advance", instance.as_deref(), &body, Duration::from_secs(60)) };
        let (status, json) = response.map_err(|error| {
            let evidence = crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange(address, "GET", "/dev/status", None, "", Duration::from_secs(5)).ok()
                .map(|(_, status)| format!("now={}, skewMs={}", status["now"], status["skewMs"]))
                .unwrap_or_else(|| "clock status unavailable".into());
            format!("clock advance reply failed at {address}: {error}; time may already have advanced ({evidence}); inspect /dev/status and queued work before retrying; for an isolated dev pass --port N")
        })?;
        if let Some(notice) = json["sessionNotice"].as_str() { eprintln!("clock: {notice}"); }
        if let Some(held) = json["held"].as_array() {
            for schedule in held.iter().filter(|s| s["holdCode"] == "saved-boundary") {
                eprintln!("clock: schedule {}: {}", schedule["name"].as_str().unwrap_or("?"), schedule["reason"].as_str().unwrap_or("held"));
            }
        }
        if let Some(denied) = json.get("denied") {
            let clock = json["message"].as_str().map(|message| format!("; time remains advanced: {message}")).unwrap_or_default();
            return Err(format!("{}: {}{clock}\n  guide: clock", denied["code"].as_str().unwrap_or("E_CLOCK_INPUT"), denied["message"].as_str().unwrap_or("clock advance failed")));
        }
        if status != 200 { return Err(format!("dev refused clock advance: {json}")); }
        Ok(json.to_string())
    })();
    match result { Ok(body) => { println!("{body}"); 0 }, Err(error) => { eprintln!("{error}"); 1 } }
}

//! Bounded, read-only evidence from the store's own commit clock.
use snapback4_core::{Engine, RuntimeError};
use std::collections::BTreeSet;

const SKIPPED_PREVIEW: usize = 32;
const TOLERANCE_MS: i64 = 5_000;
const RECENT_COMMITS: usize = 64;
const TABLE_BYTES: usize = 4096;
const TABLE_NAMES: usize = 8;
const REPORT_ERROR_BYTES: usize = 1024;
// Reserve one MiB for the outer clock/work envelope inside the host encoder.
// The reply retains `schedules` and its fired/held partition.
const REPORT_BYTE_BUDGET: usize = (crate::serve::JSON_RESPONSE_CEILING - (1 << 20)) / 2;

// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.12 — inspect a fixed recent commit window, never application row values.
pub fn ahead(engine: &Engine, now: i64) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError> {
    // Reverse primary-key traversal: no full scan, sort, row payloads or retained
    // historical stamp set. octet_length(column) uses SQLite record metadata;
    // unlike a text length/cast/substr, it need not load oversized payloads.
    let mut lead = 0;
    let mut tables = BTreeSet::new();
    let mut omitted = false;
    engine.store().visit_recent_commit_clock(now.saturating_add(TOLERANCE_MS), TABLE_BYTES as i64, RECENT_COMMITS as i64, |record| {
        let at = record.at;
        if at <= now.saturating_add(TOLERANCE_MS) { return Ok(()); }
        lead = lead.max(at.saturating_sub(now));
        let length = record.length.unwrap();
        if length > TABLE_BYTES as i64 { omitted = true; return Ok(()); }
        let bytes = record.touched.unwrap();
        match serde_json::from_slice::<Vec<String>>(&bytes) {
            Ok(names) => for name in names {
                if tables.contains(&name) { continue; }
                if tables.len() < TABLE_NAMES && name.len() <= 128 { tables.insert(name); }
                else { omitted = true; }
            },
            Err(_) => omitted = true,
        }
        Ok(())
    })?;
    if lead == 0 { return Ok(None); }
    let mut names = tables.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
    if omitted { names.push("additional tables omitted".into()); }
    if names.is_empty() { names.push("no table names recorded".into()); }
    Ok(Some(format!(
        "N_CLOCK_STORE_AHEAD: recent commit stamps lead the current clock by up to {lead}ms (latest {RECENT_COMMITS} commits; tables: {}); use a fresh store per offset test ({}), or restart with the same --clock-offset (or dev --resume-clock) to continue",
        names.join(", "), crate::dev_clock::isolated_command())))
}

/// UTC calendar text for Unix milliseconds: schedule boundaries are UTC.
pub fn utc(ms: i64) -> String {
    let (days, rem) = (ms.div_euclid(86_400_000), ms.rem_euclid(86_400_000));
    // Civil-from-days (proleptic Gregorian), exact for the I53 range.
    let z = days + 719_468;
    let era = z.div_euclid(146_097);
    let doe = z - era * 146_097;
    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1_460 + doe / 36_524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
    let day = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1;
    let month = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 };
    let year = yoe + era * 400 + i64::from(month <= 2);
    format!("{year:04}-{month:02}-{day:02}T{:02}:{:02}:{:02}Z", rem / 3_600_000, rem % 3_600_000 / 60_000, rem % 60_000 / 1_000)
}

/// A positive duration in the units `clock advance` accepts, rounded up to a second.
pub fn span(ms: i64) -> String {
    let seconds = (ms.max(0) + 999) / 1_000;
    let (d, h, m, s) = (seconds / 86_400, seconds % 86_400 / 3_600, seconds % 3_600 / 60, seconds % 60);
    let parts: Vec<String> = [(d, "d"), (h, "h"), (m, "m"), (s, "s")].into_iter().filter(|(n, _)| *n > 0).map(|(n, unit)| format!("{n}{unit}")).collect();
    if parts.is_empty() { "0s".into() } else { parts.join("") }
}

/// Each schedule's saved boundary, in declaration order.
pub fn saved_boundaries(engine: &Engine) -> Vec<Option<i64>> {
    engine.schema().schedules.iter()
        .map(|schedule| {
            let shape = engine.store().schedule_shape(&schedule.name).ok().flatten();
            if shape.as_ref().is_some_and(|shape| *shape != snapback4_core::value::digest(schedule)) { return None; }
            engine.store().schedule_boundary(&schedule.name).ok().flatten()
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Preflight is bounded before the clock or worker leases change.
// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.12.1 — only explicit execution enumerates all crossed windows; coalesced reports keep a bounded preview.
pub fn crossed_boundaries(engine: &Engine, before: &[Option<i64>], now: i64, held: bool, each_boundary: bool) -> Result<Vec<(usize, i64)>, snapback4_core::Refusal> {
    let mut boundaries = Vec::new();
    let mut report_bytes = 0usize;
    for (index, schedule) in engine.schema().schedules.iter().enumerate() {
        // JSON may escape every error byte; count that bound per schedule.
        report_bytes = report_bytes.saturating_add(2048 + 6 * (REPORT_ERROR_BYTES + 3) + 8 * (schedule.name.len() + schedule.target.len()));
        if report_bytes > REPORT_BYTE_BUDGET { return Err(crate::dev_clock::input("schedule report exceeds its byte budget; reduce the declared schedules")); }
        if held { continue; }
        let Some(old) = before.get(index).copied().flatten() else { continue; };
        let end = schedule.boundary(now);
        if old >= end { continue; }
        let periods = schedule.periods_between(old, end);
        if each_boundary && periods > (10_000 - boundaries.len()) as i64 {
            return Err(crate::dev_clock::input("--each-boundary crosses more than 10000 schedule windows; use a smaller duration or omit --each-boundary to coalesce"));
        }
        report_bytes = report_bytes.saturating_add((if each_boundary { periods as usize } else { (periods as usize).min(SKIPPED_PREVIEW + 1) }).saturating_mul(1024 + 8 * schedule.target.len()));
        if report_bytes > REPORT_BYTE_BUDGET { return Err(crate::dev_clock::input("schedule window report exceeds its byte budget; use a smaller duration")); }
        if !each_boundary { continue; }
        let mut boundary = schedule.next(old);
        while boundary <= end {
            boundaries.push((index, boundary));
            boundary = schedule.next(boundary);
        }
    }
    boundaries.sort_by_key(|(index, at)| (*at, *index));
    Ok(boundaries)
}

fn period(schedule: &snapback4_core::schema::Schedule) -> String {
    schedule.describe()
}

/// What each schedule did on one clock advance, and why one did not fire.
/// The core fires each schedule at most once per advance, for the latest
/// boundary, and holds it while its saved boundary is ahead of the clock.
// @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — missed boundaries fire once; this only explains them.
pub fn schedule_report(engine: &Engine, before: &[Option<i64>], fired: &[String], now: i64, held: bool, each_boundary: bool, port: Option<u16>) -> Vec<serde_json::Value> {
    let after = saved_boundaries(engine);
    // Read only bounded summaries: job args/cursors and full error payloads
    // are irrelevant to this report and must not be loaded then replicated.
    let runs = job_summaries(engine).unwrap_or_default();
    engine.schema().schedules.iter().enumerate().map(|(index, schedule)| {
        let (old, saved) = (before.get(index).copied().flatten(), after.get(index).copied().flatten());
        let current = schedule.boundary(now);
        let next = schedule.next(current);
        let mut entry = serde_json::json!({ "name": schedule.name, "target": schedule.target, "period": period(schedule), "fired": false, "firedWindows": [], "skippedBoundaries": [], "nextBoundary": utc(next) });
        if fired.contains(&schedule.name) {
            let end = saved.unwrap_or(current);
            entry["fired"] = true.into();
            let start = schedule.previous(end);
            let window = |boundary| serde_json::json!({"periodStart": schedule.previous(boundary), "periodEnd": boundary});
            let mut windows = Vec::new();
            if each_boundary {
                if let Some(old) = old {
                    let mut at = schedule.next(old);
                    while at <= end { windows.push(window(at)); at = schedule.next(at); }
                }
            } else { windows.push(window(end)); }
            if each_boundary {
                entry["reason"] = format!("fired {} windows: {}", windows.len(), windows.iter().map(|window| format!("{} to {}", utc(window["periodStart"].as_i64().unwrap()), utc(window["periodEnd"].as_i64().unwrap()))).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("; ")).into();
            }
            entry["firedWindows"] = windows.into();
            entry["periodStart"] = start.into();
            entry["periodEnd"] = end.into();
            if !each_boundary { entry["reason"] = format!("fired for the period {} to {}", utc(start), utc(end)).into(); }
            if let Some(run) = runs.get(&schedule.target) { entry["run"] = run.clone(); }
            // @ref LLP 3000.040#24-monthly-and-yearly-schedules — calendar periods count boundaries, not milliseconds.
            let skipped = if each_boundary { 0 } else { old.map(|old| schedule.periods_between(old, end) - 1).unwrap_or(0) };
            if skipped > 0 {
                entry["skippedPeriods"] = skipped.into();
                let mut windows = Vec::new();
                let mut at = schedule.next(old.unwrap());
                while at < end && windows.len() < SKIPPED_PREVIEW {
                    let mut item = window(at);
                    let mut args = serde_json::Map::new();
                    if let Some(program) = engine.program(&schedule.target) {
                        if program.args.contains_key("periodStart") { args.insert("periodStart".into(), schedule.previous(at).into()); }
                        if program.args.contains_key("periodEnd") { args.insert("periodEnd".into(), at.into()); }
                    }
                    item["command"] = format!("snapback4 run {} '{}'{}", schedule.target, serde_json::Value::Object(args), port.map(|port| format!(" --port {port}")).unwrap_or_default()).into();
                    windows.push(item); at = schedule.next(at);
                }
                entry["skippedBoundariesOmitted"] = (skipped - windows.len() as i64).into();
                entry["skippedBoundaries"] = windows.into();
                entry["reason"] = format!("fired once, for the latest period {} to {}; {skipped} earlier period{} this advance crossed (from {}) did not run: missed boundaries fire once. Run {} with periodStart/periodEnd for an earlier period",
                    utc(start), utc(end), if skipped == 1 { "" } else { "s" }, utc(old.unwrap_or(end)), schedule.target).into();
            }
        } else if held {
            entry["holdCode"] = "disabled".into();
            entry["reason"] = "schedules are held (dev --hold-schedules or --replay); a restart without the flag resumes at the next boundary".into();
        } else if let Some(saved) = saved.filter(|saved| old.is_some() && (*saved > current || *saved == current && *saved > schedule.boundary(snapback4_core::now_ms()))) {
            let due = schedule.next(saved);
            entry["holdCode"] = "saved-boundary".into();
            entry["savedBoundary"] = saved.into();
            entry["heldUntil"] = utc(due).into();
            entry["nextBoundary"] = utc(due).into();
            entry["reason"] = format!("held by the store: boundary {} was already processed and this clock {} has not reached its next window (restarting resets the process offset, not the saved boundary). One fire per boundary. Advance {} more, or use a fresh staging deployment/store for an independent test; keep the same --clock-offset when continuing a test across serve restarts",
                utc(saved), utc(now), span(due - now)).into();
        } else if old != saved {
            entry["holdCode"] = "initialized".into();
            entry["reason"] = format!("{} started at boundary {}: a schedule fires at the boundary after the first one it sees, next {} ({} from now)",
                if old.is_none() { "this schedule" } else { "this changed schedule" }, utc(saved.unwrap_or(current)), utc(next), span(next - now)).into();
        } else {
            entry["holdCode"] = "not-due".into();
            entry["reason"] = format!("next boundary {} ({} from now; schedule times are UTC)", utc(next), span(next - now)).into();
        }
        entry
    }).collect()
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#10-wave-20-loop-repairs-dx5 — every declared schedule has one reported outcome.
pub fn outcomes(schedules: &[serde_json::Value]) -> (Vec<serde_json::Value>, Vec<serde_json::Value>) {
    schedules.iter().cloned().partition(|schedule| schedule["fired"] == true)
}

/// The report never loads full error/argument payloads from retained jobs.
fn job_summaries(engine: &Engine) -> Result<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value>, RuntimeError> {
    let mut summaries = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
    for summary in engine.store().job_summaries(REPORT_ERROR_BYTES)? {
        let name = summary.name;
        if summaries.contains_key(&name) { continue; }
        let mut error = summary.error;
        let truncated = summary.error_truncated;
        if let Some(text) = &mut error && truncated {
            let mut end = REPORT_ERROR_BYTES.min(text.len());
            while !text.is_char_boundary(end) { end -= 1; }
            text.truncate(end); text.push('…');
        }
        summaries.insert(name, serde_json::json!({ "id":summary.id, "state":summary.state,
            "rowsWritten":summary.rows_written, "error":error, "errorTruncated":truncated }));
    }
    Ok(summaries)
}

/// Startup lines for schedules the store holds: their saved boundary leads the clock.
pub fn held_schedules(engine: &Engine, now: i64) -> Vec<String> {
    engine.schema().schedules.iter().zip(saved_boundaries(engine)).filter_map(|(schedule, saved)| {
        let saved = saved.filter(|saved| *saved > schedule.boundary(now))?;
        let due = schedule.next(saved);
        Some(format!("clock     schedule {} is held until {} ({} from now): its saved boundary {} is ahead of this clock; `clock advance {}` or restart with dev --resume-clock",
            schedule.name, utc(due), span(due - now), utc(saved), span(due - now)))
    }).collect()
}

/// The dev clock offset that continues a store's own time: its newest
/// recent commit stamp (or saved schedule boundary) less wall time, never negative.
pub fn resume_offset(store: &snapback4_core::Store, wall: i64) -> Result<i64, RuntimeError> {
    let commit = store.recent_commit_max_at(RECENT_COMMITS as i64)?;
    let boundary = store.latest_schedule_boundary()?;
    let latest = commit.into_iter().chain(boundary).max().unwrap_or(wall);
    // Whole seconds, rounded up, so restarting twice does not drift backwards.
    Ok((latest.saturating_sub(wall).max(0) + 999) / 1_000 * 1_000)
}

pub fn has_data(engine: &Engine) -> bool {
    engine.store().inspection_has_data().unwrap_or(false)
}

pub fn offset_line(offset: i64, running: bool) -> String {
    format!("clock     offset from wall time: {offset:+}ms{}", if running { " (lasts until restart)" } else { " (no running dev; inspecting against wall time)" })
}

        engine.fire_schedules(0).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(crossed_boundaries(&engine, &before, 60_000, false, true).unwrap().len(), 500);
        let fired = engine.fire_schedules(60_000).unwrap();
        let message = "🧪\n\\".repeat(30_000);
        engine.store().conn().execute("UPDATE _jobs SET error = ?1 WHERE id = (SELECT id FROM _jobs ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT 1)", [&message]).unwrap();
        let report = schedule_report(&engine, &before, &fired, 60_000, false, false, None);
        assert_eq!(report.len(), 500);
        assert!(report.iter().all(|s| s["run"]["errorTruncated"] == true));
        assert!(report.iter().all(|s| s["run"]["error"].as_str().unwrap().len() <= REPORT_ERROR_BYTES + 3));
        assert!(serde_json::to_vec(&report).unwrap().len() < 2 << 20);
    }
    #[test]
    fn clock_report_refuses_before_the_host_encoder_limit() {
        let mut source = "table rows:\n  n: int\n  public 'fixture'\njob tick():\n  for row in rows:\n    update rows[row.id] {n:1}\n".to_owned();

    }

    }

        seed(&mut engine, "beta", 107_000, 3_000_000);
        let note = ahead(&engine, 100_000).unwrap().unwrap();
        assert!(note.contains("up to 7000ms (latest 64 commits; tables: beta)"), "{note}");
        let note = ahead(&engine, 99_999).unwrap().unwrap();
        assert!(note.contains("up to 7001ms (latest 64 commits; tables: alpha, beta)"), "{note}");
        assert!(ahead(&engine, 102_000).unwrap().is_none());
    }
    #[test]
    fn recent_window_does_not_claim_older_commits_or_read_row_payloads() {

        engine.store().conn().execute("UPDATE r SET data = 'not json'", []).unwrap();
        assert!(ahead(&engine, 100_000).unwrap().is_none());
        engine.store().conn().execute("UPDATE _commits SET at = 200000, touched = ?1 WHERE seq = (SELECT MAX(seq) FROM _commits)", ["x".repeat(TABLE_BYTES + 1)]).unwrap();
        let note = ahead(&engine, 100_000).unwrap().unwrap();
        assert!(note.contains("100000ms") && note.contains("additional tables omitted"), "{note}");
    }
}

/** Starts a release. stop() awaits native exit and kernel store release.
 * @throws E_PROOF_USAGE for missing deployment directory; child exit, readiness deadline or served identity mismatch. stop() rejects bounded cleanup failure. */
export async function startServe(deployDir: string, options: ServeOptions | readonly string[] = {}): Promise<ServeHost> {
  if (typeof deployDir !== "string" || !deployDir.trim()) throw Object.assign(new TypeError("E_PROOF_USAGE: startServe(deployDir, options) requires a deployment directory as its first argument"), { code: "E_PROOF_USAGE" });

  const directory = resolve(opts.cwd ?? ".", deployDir);

  if (opts.clockOffset !== undefined && opts.args?.some(arg => arg === "--clock-offset" || arg.startsWith("--clock-offset="))) throw new TypeError("E_PROOF_USAGE: pass clockOffset once");
  const host = await nativeHost("serve", [directory], { ...opts, args: [...(opts.args ?? []), ...(opts.clockOffset === undefined ? [] : ["--clock-offset", opts.clockOffset])] });
  const clockCall = async (body?: object): Promise<ClockAdvance> => {
    const config = await fetchIdentity(`${host.url}/auth/config`, deadline(opts.timeoutMs, 10_000));
    if (!config.response.ok || config.body.environment !== "staging") throw Error("E_CLOCK_DEV_ONLY: clock controls require a deploy --staging store");
    const clockToken = served.operatorToken("clock");
    const response = await fetch(`${host.url}/dev/clock/${body ? "advance" : "status"}`, { method: body ? "POST" : "GET", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${await clockToken}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, ...(body ? { body: JSON.stringify(body) } : {}), signal: AbortSignal.timeout(deadline(opts.timeoutMs, 60_000)) });
    const result = await response.json() as Partial<ClockAdvance> & { sessionNotice?: string; denied?: { code?: string; message?: string } };
    if (result.sessionNotice) process.stderr.write(`snapback4: ${result.sessionNotice}\n`);
    if (!response.ok || result.denied || !Number.isSafeInteger(result.now)) throw Object.assign(Error(`staging clock refused or reply unavailable; inspect clock and queued work before retrying: ${result.denied?.code ?? response.status} ${result.denied?.message ?? ""}`), { report: result });
    if (body && (!Array.isArray(result.fired) || !Array.isArray(result.held))) throw Error("staging clock reply has no schedule report; inspect clock and queued work before retrying");
    for (const schedule of result.held ?? []) if (schedule.holdCode === "saved-boundary") process.stderr.write(`snapback4: schedule ${schedule.name}: ${schedule.reason}\n`);
    return { now: result.now!, fired: result.fired ?? [], held: result.held ?? [] };
  };
  // Exit can precede inherited watchdog flock release. The private local
  // barrier observes the same canonical ownership sidecar without writing data.
  let stopping: Promise<void> | undefined;
  const stop = () => stopping ??= (async () => {
    await host.stop();
    const result = await cli(["serve", directory, "--wait-stopped"], {...opts, timeoutMs:6000});
    if (result.code !== 0) throw Error(`proof serve store release failed: ${result.stderr}`);
  })().catch(error => { stopping = undefined; throw error; });
  const served: ServeHost = { ...host, stop,
    now: async () => (await clockCall()).now,
    advance: (duration, options = {}) => {
      if (typeof duration !== "string" || !/^\+?\d+(ms|s|m|h|d|w)$/.test(duration)) throw new TypeError("E_PROOF_USAGE: advance requires a positive whole duration");
      return clockCall({ duration, eachBoundary: options.eachBoundary ?? false });
    },
    operatorToken: async (service = "operator", days = 1) => {
      if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/.test(service) || !Number.isSafeInteger(days) || days < 1 || days > 3650) throw Error("proof operatorToken: invalid service or days (1..3650)");
      const result = await cli(["token", "--service", service, "--days", String(days), "--release", directory, "--quiet"], opts);
      if (result.code !== 0) throw Error(`proof operator token refused: ${result.stderr}`);
      const token = result.stdout.trim();
      if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/.test(token)) throw Error("proof operator token malformed");
      return token;
    },
    seedAccounts: accountOptions => seedAccounts(served, accountOptions),
  };
  try { if (opts.seedUsers) served.sessions = await served.seedAccounts(opts.seedUsers); return served; }
  catch (error) { await served.stop(); throw error; }
}

export interface CliResult { code: number | null; signal: NodeJS.Signals | null; stdout: string; stderr: string; logs: ProofHost["logs"] }
/** Waits for close (stdio drained), never merges the two streams. Nonzero is returned for refusal assertions. */
/** @throws spawn error or command deadline; nonzero exit is returned in code, not thrown. */
export function cli(args: readonly string[], options: ProofOptions = {}): Promise<CliResult> {
  return command(process.execPath, [fileURLToPath(new URL("../bin/snapback4.js", import.meta.url)), ...args], { ...options, secret: options.secret || args[0] === "token" });
}
/** A bounded directly spawned build/tool command, with the same file logs. */
/** @throws spawn error or command deadline; nonzero exit is returned in code, not thrown. */
export async function command(binary: string, args: readonly string[], options: ProofOptions = {}): Promise<CliResult> {
  const run = logged(binary, args, { ...options, env: { ...process.env, ...options.env } });
  try {
    await bounded(run.closed, deadline(options.timeoutMs, 120_000), "proof cli close");
    if (run.error()) throw run.error();
    return { code: run.child.exitCode, signal: run.child.signalCode, stdout: run.stdout(), stderr: logText(run.logs.stderr), logs: run.logs };
  } catch (error) { await stopChild(run.child, deadline(options.stopTimeoutMs, 5000)); throw error; }
  finally { run.child.stdout?.destroy(); } // Secret capture must not pin the driver after a deadline.
}
async function successful(args: string[], options: ProofOptions) {
  const result = await cli(args, options);
  if (result.code !== 0) {
    const stdout = result.stdout.trimEnd();
    const tail = stdout.length > 4000 ? `…${stdout.slice(-4000)}` : stdout;
    throw Error(`proof CLI failed (${result.code}): ${result.stderr}; stdout tail: ${tail || "(empty)"}; logs: ${result.logs.stderr}`);
  }
  return result;
}

export function deploy(dir: string, schema: string, options: ProofOptions = {}) {
  if (typeof schema !== "string" || !schema) throw Error(`proof deploy requires an explicit saved schema file or directory; got ${JSON.stringify(schema) ?? String(schema)}: did npm run day2:proof pass versions/v1?`);
  return successful(["deploy", dir, "--schema", schema, ...(options.args ?? [])], options);
}
/** @throws invalid explicit release target, CLI failure, spawn error or deadline. */
export function rollback(dir: string, to: number | "latest", options: ProofOptions = {}) {
  if (to !== "latest" && (!Number.isSafeInteger(to) || to < 1)) throw Error(`proof rollback requires an explicit immutable release target; got ${JSON.stringify(to) ?? String(to)}`);
  return successful(["rollback", dir, "--to", String(to), ...(options.args ?? [])], options);
}

    try { cases = JSON.parse(summaries[0]![1]!) as { run: number; skipped: number }; }
    catch { throw Error(`proof testSource received a malformed business-case summary: ${summaries[0]![0]}; logs: ${result.logs.stdout}`); }
    if (!Number.isSafeInteger(cases.run) || cases.run < 0 || !Number.isSafeInteger(cases.skipped) || cases.skipped < 0) {
      throw Error(`proof testSource received invalid business-case counts: ${summaries[0]![0]}; logs: ${result.logs.stdout}`);
    }
    if (cases.run === 0 && !fixtureOnly) {
      throw Error(`proof testSource ran no business cases (${cases.skipped} skipped); add test.cases.jsonl for this saved version, or pass { fixtureOnly: true } when fixture loading alone is the intended proof; stdout tail: ${result.stdout.trimEnd().slice(-4000) || "(empty)"}`);
    }
    return { ...result, casesRun: cases.run, casesSkipped: cases.skipped };
  });
}

}

fn completed_drain(work: Work, stopping: bool) -> Result<Work, snapback4_core::Refusal> {
    if stopping {
        return Err(snapback4_core::Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_INTERRUPTED", "clock", "clock advanced, but host shutdown interrupted the drain; inspect queued work instead of repeating the advance").guide("clock"));
    }
    Ok(work)
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#4-staging-clock — staging grants clock control, never fixture or persona authority.
pub(super) fn staging(shared: &Shared) -> bool {
    lock(&shared.engine).store().meta("deployment_environment").ok().flatten().as_deref() == Some("staging")
}
fn clock_service(request: &Request, shared: &Shared) -> Result<Option<String>, snapback4_core::Refusal> {
    if shared.personas { return Ok(None); }
    if !staging(shared) { return Err(crate::dev_clock::release()); }
    match super::session_identity::principal_of(request,shared) {
        Ok((principal,kind,snapback4_core::identity::SessionScope::Full)) if kind == "service" && principal.starts_with("service:") => Ok(Some(principal)),
        _ => Err(snapback4_core::Refusal::new("E_AUTH", "auth", "staging clock control requires a full service token").guide("clock")),
    }
}
pub(super) fn advance(request: Request, shared: &Shared, body: &str) {
    let service = match clock_service(&request, shared) {
        Ok(service) => service,
        Err(why) => return respond(request,403,json!({"denied":refusal_json(&why)})),
    };
    let payload = match serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(body) {
        Ok(payload) => payload,
        Err(_) => return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&crate::dev_clock::input("clock advance takes {\"duration\":\"+2m\"}"))})),
    };
    let each_boundary = match payload.get("eachBoundary") {
        None => false,
        Some(serde_json::Value::Bool(value)) => *value,
        Some(_) => return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&crate::dev_clock::input("eachBoundary must be a boolean"))})),
    };
    let duration = payload.get("duration").and_then(|value| value.as_str());
    let milliseconds = match duration.ok_or_else(|| crate::dev_clock::input("clock advance takes {\"duration\":\"+2m\"}"))
        .and_then(crate::dev_clock::duration) {
        Ok(milliseconds) => milliseconds,
        Err(error) => return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error)})),
    };
    // Serialize clock callers only. Background slices check advancing after
    // engine admission and skip during this synchronous drain.
    let advance = lock(&shared.maintenance).advance.clone();
    let _advance = lock(&advance);
    let _advancing = Advancing(shared);
    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.12 — simulated time makes retries due without stealing a live worker's claim or viewer session.
    let advanced = (|| {
        // Match claims' engine-then-clock lock order: no claim can land
        // between shifting its lease and publishing the advanced clock.
        let mut engine = lock(&shared.engine);
        let before = crate::dev_clock_store::saved_boundaries(&engine);
        if let Some(principal) = &service {
            if engine.store().meta("deployment_environment").map_err(|e|e.refusal())?.as_deref() != Some("staging") { return Err(crate::dev_clock::release()); }
            super::session_identity::mutation_authority(&request,shared,&engine,principal)?;
        } else { shared.dev_authority(&engine)?; }
        let mut clock = lock(&shared.clock);
        let mut next = clock.clone();
        let now = next.advance(milliseconds)?.max(shared.time_audience_clock.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire));
        let boundaries = crate::dev_clock_store::crossed_boundaries(&engine, &before, now, shared.hold_schedules, each_boundary)?;
        lock(&shared.maintenance).advancing = true;
        engine.advance_worker_leases_at(milliseconds, clock.now()).map_err(|e| e.refusal())?;
        *clock = next;
        let offset = clock.offset();
        let skew = now - snapback4_core::now_ms();
        let isolated = if crate::dev_clock_store::has_data(&engine) {
            format!("; use {} for isolated time tests; clock advance --port N targets its printed port (guide jobs)", crate::dev_clock::isolated_command())
        } else { String::new() };
        let message = format!("cumulative offset {offset:+}ms (requested process offset; now includes the authoritative floor); process offset lasts until restart{isolated}");
        Ok((now, offset, skew, message, before, boundaries))
    })();
    let (now, offset, skew, message, before, boundaries) = match advanced {
        Ok(result) => result,
        Err(error) => return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error)})),
    };
    // @ref LLP 3000#contended-read-serving — a developer is awaiting this
    // request; synchronous clock-advance work intentionally keeps request QoS.
    let drained = (|| {
        let mut crossed = Vec::new();
        if each_boundary {
            for (index, at) in boundaries {
                crossed.extend(engine_work(shared, |engine, _| engine.fire_schedule_boundary_at(shared.now(), index, at))?);
            }
        }
        let mut work = work_at(shared, true, 0, Some(now))?;
        work.schedules += crossed.len();
        work.fired.extend(crossed);
        Ok::<_, RuntimeError>(work)
    })();
    match drained.map_err(|error| error.refusal()).and_then(|work| completed_drain(work, crate::lifecycle::stopping())) {
        Ok(work) => {
            let schedules = crate::dev_clock_store::schedule_report(&lock(&shared.engine), &before, &work.fired, now, shared.hold_schedules, each_boundary, shared.dev_identity.as_ref().map(|i| i.address.port()));
            let (fired, held) = crate::dev_clock_store::outcomes(&schedules);
            respond(request, 200, json!({"now":now, "advancedMs":milliseconds, "sessionNotice":crate::dev_clock::SESSION_NOTICE, "offsetMs":offset, "skewMs":skew, "eachBoundary":each_boundary, "message":message, "work":work, "schedules":schedules, "fired":fired, "held":held}))
        }
        // Time remains advanced if maintenance fails; callers must not
        // retry the advance blindly. The normal tick retries pending work.
        Err(error) => {
            let engine = lock(&shared.engine);
            let after = crate::dev_clock_store::saved_boundaries(&engine);
            let fired: Vec<_> = engine.schema().schedules.iter().enumerate().filter(|(i, _)| {
                matches!((before.get(*i).copied().flatten(), after.get(*i).copied().flatten()), (Some(old), Some(new)) if new > old)
            }).map(|(_, schedule)| schedule.name.clone()).collect();
            let mut schedules = crate::dev_clock_store::schedule_report(&engine, &before, &fired, now, shared.hold_schedules, each_boundary, shared.dev_identity.as_ref().map(|i| i.address.port()));
            for (index, schedule) in schedules.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                if schedule["fired"] != true && !shared.hold_schedules && before.get(index).copied().flatten().is_some_and(|old| old < engine.schema().schedules[index].boundary(now)) {
                    schedule["holdCode"] = "maintenance-failed".into();
                    schedule["reason"] = "clock advanced but maintenance stopped before this due boundary was queued; inspect clock and queued jobs before continuing; do not replay the advance".into();
                }
            }
            let (fired, held) = crate::dev_clock_store::outcomes(&schedules);
            respond(request, 500, json!({"now":now, "advancedMs":milliseconds, "sessionNotice":crate::dev_clock::SESSION_NOTICE, "offsetMs":offset, "skewMs":skew, "eachBoundary":each_boundary, "message":message, "schedules":schedules, "fired":fired, "held":held, "reportIncomplete":true, "denied":refusal_json(&error)}))
        },
    }
}

    };

        Ok(payload) => payload,
        Err(error) => return refuse(request, 400, Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("the request body is not JSON: {error}; send {{\"args\":{{..}}}}"))),
    };

 * Mount route-owned child components only while their route is active. Unmount
 * releases this owner; keep:true still permits its existing 30-second linger.
 * Account/backend/argument keys belong to the shell. The bounded screen recipe
 * in CLIENT-AND-OPERATIONS.md also resets page/identity owners on withdrawal,
 * including generation changes. There is no inactive Read or query cache.
 * @ref LLP 3000.023#13 — tested route-owned composition before another hook option.
 */
export function useQuery<A, R>(op: Query<A, R>, args: A, options?: ReadHookOptions): Read<R> {
  const client = useClient();
  const skip = options?.skip === true;
  const key = skip ? null : readKey(op, args);
  const observed = useMemo(() => skip ? SKIPPED_READ as Observed<R> : new Observation(
    () => client.observe(op, args, observeOptions(options)),
    () => peekObservation(client, op, args, observeOptions(options))), [client, op, key, options?.keep, skip]); // eslint-disable-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  return useSyncExternalStore(observed.subscribe, observed.getSnapshot, () => LOADING as Read<R>);
}

/** A refused data-only query. Error boundaries can render `why.message`. */
// @ref LLP 3000.013.002#2 — refusals must not look like an endless loading state.
export class QueryRefusal extends Error {
  constructor(readonly why: Refusal) { super(why.message); this.name = "QueryRefusal"; }
}

/** Render a list read or page in one expression. Empty describes returned
 * rows, including partial/stale answers; it never proves absence. This owns
 * no observation and does not retain a previous read. Native callers supply
 * Text/View elements in the same slots. A missing denied renderer throws the
 * original typed QueryRefusal for an error boundary. */
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#10-wave-20-loop-repairs-dx5 — presentation preserves precise read evidence.
export function ReadState<R extends readonly unknown[]>({ read: source, loading = null, empty = null, denied, children }: {
  read: Read<R> | { read: Read<R> };
  loading?: ReactNode;
  empty?: ReactNode;
  denied?: (why: Refusal) => ReactNode;
  children: (items: R, read: Ready<R>) => ReactNode;
}): ReactNode {
  const read = "read" in source ? source.read : source;
  if ("denied" in read) {
    if (denied) return denied(read.denied);
    throw new QueryRefusal(read.denied);
  }
  if (!("data" in read)) return loading;
  return read.data.length === 0 ? empty : children(read.data, read);
}

/** Authorized data as it arrives, undefined while loading. Null and empty
 * arrays remain data. Partial/stale answers remain data too: use useQuery or
 * usePage when completeness, freshness or continuation matters. Refusals throw
 * QueryRefusal; useQueryResult instead for an inline typed refusal. */
export function useQueryData<A, R>(op: Query<A, R>, args: A, options?: ReadHookOptions): R | undefined {
  const read = useQuery(op, args, options);
  if ("denied" in read) throw new QueryRefusal(read.denied);
  return "data" in read ? read.data : undefined;
}

/** The same observation with an inline refusal and its precise metadata. */
export function useQueryResult<A, R>(op: Query<A, R>, args: A, options?: ReadHookOptions): {
  readonly data: R | undefined; readonly why: Refusal | null; readonly read: Read<R>;
} {
  const read = useQuery(op, args, options);
  return { data: "data" in read ? read.data : undefined, why: "denied" in read ? read.denied : null, read };
}

//! Query result paths and nullable reads of private side tables.
use super::*;

pub(super) const VIEWER_KEY: &str = "$lookupViewerKey";
const TARGET_ROW: &str = "$lookupTargetRow";

// @ref LLP 3000.036.002#151-evidence-and-decision — compatibility keeps
// fallthrough null; check must name a concrete uncovered source path.
pub(super) fn fallthrough(decl: &ast::ProgramDecl) -> Diagnostic {
    fn path(body: &[S], implicit: bool) -> Option<Vec<String>> {
        let mut route = Vec::new();
        for (at, stmt) in body.iter().enumerate() {
            match stmt {
                S::Return { .. } => return None,
                S::Expr { .. } if implicit && at + 1 == body.len() => return None,
                S::Require { condition: A::Literal { value: Literal::Bool(false), .. }, .. } => return None,
                S::If { then_body, else_body, site, .. } => {
                    let completes = implicit && at + 1 == body.len();
                    let (arm, rest) = if let Some(rest) = path(then_body, completes) { ("true", rest) }
                        else if let Some(rest) = path(else_body, completes) { ("false", rest) }
                        else { return None };
                    route.push(format!("if at {site} is {arm}")); route.extend(rest);
                }
                S::For { site, .. } => route.push(format!("loop at {site} has zero iterations")),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Some(route)
    }
    let route = path(&decl.body, true).unwrap_or_default();
    let route = if route.is_empty() { "entry → end".into() } else { format!("{} → end", route.join(" → ")) };
    Diagnostic::new(&decl.site, "N_QUERY_FALLTHROUGH",
        format!("query {} can finish without a result ({route}); that path returns null", decl.name),
        "return a value on this path: add `return []` for an intentionally empty list, or `return null` for intentional absence; a return inside a possibly empty loop does not cover its zero-iteration path").guide("programs")
}

impl Binder<'_> {
    fn lookup_rule_proved(&self, value: &A) -> bool {
        let mut copy = value.clone();
        let mut target = false;
        super::super::intent_walk::expression(&mut copy, &mut |node| {
            if matches!(node, A::Name { name, .. } if name == TARGET_ROW) { target = true; }
        });
        if !target { return self.point_guard_safe(value) && self.authorization_proved(value, true); }
        match value {
            A::Binary { op, left, right, .. } if op == "or" => self.lookup_rule_proved(left) || self.lookup_rule_proved(right),
            A::Binary { op, left, right, .. } if op == "and" => self.lookup_rule_proved(left) && self.lookup_rule_proved(right),
            _ => false,
        }
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#152-lookup-contract-and-diagnostics — transport
    // only source advice facts across the helper's captured argument boundary.
    pub(super) fn helper_lookup_points(&self, function: &ast::FunctionDecl, args: &[A]) -> Vec<ReadExpr> {
        fn closed(value: &A, parameters: &[ast::ArgDecl]) -> bool {
            let mut value = value.clone();
            let mut safe = true;
            super::super::intent_walk::expression(&mut value, &mut |node| match node {
                A::Name { name, .. } if name != "viewer" && name != "now" && !parameters.iter().any(|p| p.name == *name) => safe = false,
                A::Focal { .. } | A::Write { .. } | A::Call { .. } => safe = false,
                _ => {}
            });
            safe
        }
        fn substitute(value: &mut A, parameters: &[ast::ArgDecl], args: &[A]) {
            super::super::intent_walk::expression(value, &mut |node| {
                if let A::Name { name, .. } = node && let Some(at) = parameters.iter().position(|p| p.name == *name)
                    && let Some(argument) = args.get(at) { *node = argument.clone(); }
            });
        }
        fn collect(catalog: &Catalog, function: &ast::FunctionDecl, args: &[A], stack: &mut Vec<String>, fuel: &mut usize, reads: &mut Vec<ReadExpr>) {
            if stack.len() >= 32 || stack.contains(&function.name) { return; }
            stack.push(function.name.clone());
            let mut body = match &function.body { ast::FunctionBody::Block(body) => body.clone(), ast::FunctionBody::Expression(value) => vec![S::Return { value: value.clone(), site: value.site().clone() }] };
            super::super::intent_walk::statements(&mut body, &mut |node| {
                if *fuel == 0 { return; } *fuel -= 1;
                match node {
                    A::Read(read) if read.keys.iter().all(|key| closed(&key.value, &function.args)) => {
                        let mut value = A::Read(read.clone()); substitute(&mut value, &function.args, args);
                        if let A::Read(read) = value { reads.push(read); }
                    }
                    A::Call { name, args: arguments, .. } if arguments.iter().all(|value| closed(value, &function.args)) => {
                        if let Some(callee) = catalog.functions.get(name) {
                            let mut arguments = arguments.clone();
                            for value in &mut arguments { substitute(value, &function.args, args); }
                            collect(catalog, callee, &arguments, stack, fuel, reads);
                        }
                    }
                    _ => {}
                }
            });
            stack.pop();
        }
        if self.caller_kind != ProgramKind::Mutation { return Vec::new(); }
        let identity: Vec<_> = function.args.iter().map(|p| A::Name { name: p.name.clone(), site: p.site.clone() }).collect();
        let mut reads = Vec::new();
        collect(self.catalog, function, &identity, &mut Vec::new(), &mut 512, &mut reads);
        reads.into_iter().filter(|read| read.keys.iter().all(|key| closed(&key.value, &function.args))).filter(|read| {
            let mut value = A::Read(read.clone()); substitute(&mut value, &function.args, args);
            let A::Read(actual) = value else { return false };
            self.point_guard_safe(&A::Read(actual.clone())) && (self.point_present(&actual) || self.lookup_point_present(&actual) || self.row_independent_read_proved(&actual.table))
        }).collect()
    }
    // This marker suppresses advice only; it cannot authorize a runtime read
    // or enter the binder's authority/presence proof domains.
    pub(super) fn lookup_viewer_key(&self, value: &A) -> bool {
        if matches!(value, A::Name { name, .. } if name == "viewer" || self.binding(name)
            .is_some_and(|binding| binding.fields.contains_key(&vec![VIEWER_KEY.into()]))) { return true; }
        let equal = A::Binary { op: "=".into(), left: Box::new(value.clone()), right: Box::new(A::Name { name: "viewer".into(), site: value.site().clone() }), site: value.site().clone() };
        self.point_guard_safe(value) && self.authorization_proved(&equal, true)
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#10-wave-20-loop-repairs-dx5 — asserted and same-table reads still need reader authority; blind writes do not pass here.
    pub(super) fn optional_lookup_note(&mut self, read: &ReadExpr, point: &Read) {
        if self.caller_kind != ProgramKind::Mutation || self.point_present(read) || self.lookup_point_present(read)
            || self.row_independent_read_proved(&read.table) { return; }
        let table = &self.schema.tables[&read.table];
        if table.ephemeral.is_some() || self.schema.maintain_for(&read.table).is_some() { return; }
        let index = &table.indexes[&point.index];
        let pinned = index.components.iter().zip(&point.key).filter_map(|(part, value)| part.column().map(|name| (name, value))).collect();
        if snapback4_core::engine::rules::prefix_visibility(&read.table, table, &table.rules.read, &pinned).decided_true { return; }
        if let Some(rule) = self.catalog.tables[&read.table].decl.rules.iter().find(|rule| rule.effect == ast::Effect::Read) {
            let named = read.keys.iter().all(|key| key.column.is_some());
            let keys: BTreeMap<_, _> = read.keys.iter().enumerate().filter_map(|(at, key)|
                Some((if named { key.column.clone()? } else { index.components.get(at)?.column()?.clone() },

                if let A::Member { base, .. } = value && let A::Focal { site } = base.as_ref() {
                    **base = A::Name { name: TARGET_ROW.into(), site: site.clone() };
                }
            });
            super::super::intent_walk::expression(&mut condition, &mut |value| {
                if let A::Member { base, name, .. } = value && matches!(base.as_ref(), A::Name { name, .. } if name == TARGET_ROW)
                    && let Some(key) = keys.get(name) { *value = key.clone(); }
            });
            if self.lookup_rule_proved(&condition) { return; }
        }
        let rule = table.through.as_ref().map_or_else(|| format!("read <- {}", table.rules.read.quarry()), |through| format!("read through .{}", through.reference));
        let location = self.catalog.tables[&read.table].decl.rules.iter().find(|rule| rule.effect == ast::Effect::Read)
            .map(|rule| rule.site.to_string()).unwrap_or_else(|| self.catalog.tables[&read.table].decl.site.to_string());

        self.notes.push(Diagnostic::new(&read.site, "N_LOOKUP_FILTERED",
