//! Starter leftovers on the init-first path: `init --web` (or `--expo`) wrote
//! the todo starter, then the project replaced `snapback/schema.q`. The
//! starter's own files that still match the bytes init wrote, but no longer
//! fit the schema, are leftovers: `check` names them and `init --adapt`
//! removes or rewrites them. A file the project changed is never touched.
// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000#7.2 — leftovers are judged by the starter's original bytes, never by name alone.
use super::starter::{self, Body, Platform};
use super::{OwnSchema, own_schema};
use std::path::Path;

/// One unmodified starter file that no longer fits the project's schema.
pub(crate) struct Leftover {
    pub path: &'static str,
    pub why: String,
    /// The text `init --adapt` writes; `None` removes the file.
    pub rewrite: Option<String>,
}

/// Starter operations its fixtures, cases and `Todos` screen call.
const STARTER_OPERATIONS: [&str; 4] = ["list", "add", "toggle", "remove"];

/// Whether a schema still has the starter's `todos` table and the operations
/// its fixtures, cases and `Todos` screen call.
pub(super) fn fits_todos(own: &OwnSchema) -> bool {
    own.tables.iter().any(|table| table == "todos")
        && STARTER_OPERATIONS.iter().all(|op| own.operations.iter().any(|name| name == op))
}

/// What the schema in `dir` leaves of the starter, and the advice that goes
/// with it (a sign-in the project must write by hand). No schema: nothing.
pub(crate) fn leftovers(dir: &Path) -> (Vec<Leftover>, Vec<String>) {
    let (found, advice, _) = plan(dir);
    (found, advice)
}

fn plan(dir: &Path) -> (Vec<Leftover>, Vec<String>, Vec<String>) {
    let Ok(Some(own)) = own_schema(dir) else { return (Vec::new(), Vec::new(), Vec::new()) };
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    let mut advice = Vec::new();
    let mut modified = Vec::new();
    let todos = fits_todos(&own);
    for (path, text) in starter::FIXTURES {
        let current = read(dir, path);
        if current.as_ref().is_some_and(|current| *current != super::without_design_references(text)) { modified.push(path.to_owned()); }
        if !todos && current.is_some_and(|current| current == super::without_design_references(text)) {
            let what = if path.ends_with("todos.jsonl") { "rows for the todo starter's `todos` table" } else { "cases for the todo starter's list/add/toggle/remove" };
            found.push(Leftover { path, why: format!("the unmodified {what}; your snapback/*.q has no todos table with those operations, so `snapback4 test` would refuse it"), rewrite: None });
        }
    }
    for platform in [Platform::Web, Platform::Expo] {
        if !screens(dir, platform, &own, todos, &mut found, &mut advice) {
            for path in [platform.paths().0, platform.paths().1] { if read(dir, path).is_some() { modified.push(path.to_owned()); } }
        }
    }
    if let Some(text) = read(dir, "src/native-smoke.ts") {
        let wanted = starter::native_smoke(own.identity.is_some_and(|(password, guests)| password && !guests));
        let recognized = super::proof_advice::native_template(&text);
        if recognized.is_none() { modified.push("src/native-smoke.ts".to_owned()); }
        if text != wanted && let Some((version, password)) = recognized && smoke_referenced(dir) {
            let old = text != starter::native_smoke(password);
            let why = if old {
                let mode = if password != own.identity.is_some_and(|(password, guests)| password && !guests) { "; refresh also updates its sign-in mode" } else { "" };
                format!("an older starter version ({version}; adapt can refresh it){mode}")
            } else {
                "the unmodified native smoke helper uses a different starter sign-in mode (adapt can refresh it)".into()
            };
            found.push(Leftover { path: "src/native-smoke.ts", why, rewrite: Some(wanted) });
        }
    }
    if read(dir, "src/native-smoke.ts").is_some() && !smoke_referenced(dir) {
        advice.push("info: src/native-smoke.ts has no source reference; review it before a native smoke proof".into());
    }
    if !todos && let Some(web) = [false, true].into_iter().find(|web| super::proof_advice::frontend_template(dir, *web).is_some_and(|(_, template)| template.is_none())) {
        found.push(Leftover { path: "scripts/frontend-proof.mjs", why: "the unmodified todo proof needs your screen's write assertions; keep a runnable frontend scaffold that explicitly reports the missing scenario".into(), rewrite: Some(super::proof::frontend_scaffold(web)) });
    }
    readme(dir, &own, todos, &mut found, &mut modified);
    app_json(dir, &mut found);
    expo_favicon(dir, &mut found);
    (found, advice, modified)
}

// A custom entry/component/proof can reference the helper too. Generated trees
// and dependency directories are not authored source; do not follow symlinks.
fn smoke_referenced(root: &Path) -> bool {
    fn walk(dir: &Path, helper: &Path) -> bool {
        let Ok(entries)=std::fs::read_dir(dir) else { return true; };
        for entry in entries {
            let Ok(entry)=entry else {return true;};
            let Ok(kind)=entry.file_type() else {return true;};
            let path=entry.path();
            if kind.is_symlink() {continue;}
            if kind.is_dir() {
                if !matches!(entry.file_name().to_str(),Some("node_modules"|".git"|".snapback4"|".expo"|"target"|"dist"|"build"|"generated")) && walk(&path,helper) {return true;}
            } else if path!=helper && !path.to_string_lossy().ends_with(".d.ts")
                && path.extension().and_then(|e|e.to_str()).is_some_and(|e|matches!(e,"ts"|"tsx"|"js"|"jsx"|"mjs"|"cjs")) {
                if std::fs::read_to_string(path).map_or(true,|text|text.contains("native-smoke")) {return true;}
            }
        }
        false
    }
    walk(root,&root.join("src/native-smoke.ts"))
}

## 4. Staging clock

Wave-20 reporting amendment: LLP 3000.000.000.001 §10 changes the proof
advance return to `{now, fired, held}` and explains persisted boundary holds;
operator authority and clock execution semantics below are unchanged.

Only a store durably classified staging by deploy --staging may serve with
--clock-offset. Missing/unknown classification is production. This setting
is process-local, with the same signed-duration parser and monotone elapsed
clock as dev. No serve-time mechanism can reclassify an existing production store. Restart drops the offset unless explicitly
provided again; persisted timed-disclosure floors never retreat below their captured value.

Staging exposes the existing /dev/clock/status and /dev/clock/advance only
with any full service session: these are trusted operator credentials, as for
system jobs. Production refuses even with a service token, and an explicit
production serve offset refuses with E_CLOCK_DEV_ONLY before listener startup. Account, guest, read-only and unauthenticated
requests refuse. Recheck classification and session under the engine writer
before advancing. All fixture, reset, persona and dev-job doors remain closed.
Use the same advance implementation, schedule drain and ambiguous-reply law
as dev. CLI clock advance --release DIR mints its local service authority.
startServe accepts clockOffset and exposes now()/advance() through that
operator authority; it never changes store classification. Each helper control
mints a current staging-time operator session rather than caching a credential
across arbitrary time jumps. Ordinary user sessions retain normal expiry.

Hot release activation samples `shared.now()` under its engine writer, including
the persisted disclosure floor, and passes that one time through the core's
explicit `adopt_release_at`. A live preview probes the existing filesystem owner lock independently of
HTTP bind/address hints and acquires a stopped-store lock before taking its
SQLite snapshot, retaining that lock through inspection. A rollback preview
reuses its caller's existing ownership rather than probing its own lock as a
live host.
A live preview samples time through the same-owner,
store-bound existing private status protocol; no session is minted or clock
changed. A missing existing-store ownership sidecar refuses rather than assuming a
stopped host without exclusion; ordinary rollback preview can reestablish and
reuse its canonical ownership. A revision mismatch with the private database snapshot refuses as a
racing activation. Store contents and the clock are point-in-time samples, not
a freeze of later live writes. A stopped store's cold activation/preview uses
wall time, with the existing persisted disclosure floor applied by activation.
Positive and negative staging offsets are both covered by hot/preview tests.

### 15.2 Lookup contract and diagnostics

Wave-20 advice amendment: LLP 3000.000.000.001 §10 extends N_LOOKUP_FILTERED
to asserted/same-table reads, preferring an existing N_LOOKUP_HIDDEN at the
same site; private unique source advice preserves the public refusal boundary.

Keep one point-read spelling. **`t[key]` returns the readable row or null**
for absent, hidden or expired rows. **`t[key] ! else CODE` refuses with CODE**
for the same three cases. This applies in queries and mutations and through
helpers. `exists t[key]` in a program is caller-visible; a rule's `exists`
is the separate rule-witness mechanism (§14.1). An id never grants authority.
There is no new optional-lookup operator or hidden-row error: the optional
form already exists. A later require cannot replace an earlier refusal.

Public refusal data must never distinguish hidden from missing, name a
runtime hiding clause only on a hit, disclose a key, or change a refusal's
meter according to existence. Static check diagnostics may quote authored
rules and source locations: they depend only on source, not stored rows.
Developer refusal traces remain local operator evidence. A blind write is
not a lookup and must not acquire a warning suggesting wider read access.

Extend program lookup advice beyond required same-table write targets.
**N_LOOKUP_FILTERED** identifies a mutation's optional point read of a
non-public side table (a table the operation does not write) when its key and
current binder flow facts do not prove read authority. Required direct point
reads keep existing N_LOOKUP_HIDDEN advice rather than duplicate this note;
the assertion already makes refusal explicit. It names
the operation, source point, target read rule and its declaration, and the
consequence (null before a later field/default or require).
Use the binder's actual point/key and current flow proofs, including helpers;
read-through side tables are included and name their authored inherited rule.
Ephemeral and maintained-value reads retain their specialized existing advice.
Captured helper arguments transport diagnostic-only exact-point facts (including
through nested helpers), plus known viewer identities. These markers cannot
establish runtime authority, non-null typing or prediction eligibility; key
rebinding and writes invalidate exact-point advice facts. The transfer walk is
bounded (512 visited expression nodes, depth 32); exhaustion declines the
suppression proof, never a runtime read or authority check;
never infer the read from a blind write target. Exact key pins that decide
read authority, a dominating readable lookup/guard, direct asserted reads and
lookups of the operation's written tables stay quiet. Rule constants are normalized before key substitution, and the target-row
namespace is sealed before injecting caller expressions: an unpinned target
field cannot borrow an enclosing shape's focal row or a caller binding.
This is missing-proof advice, not a claim all callers are denied. Repeated instances
are located, and advice suggests a deliberately reader-visible projection or
an earlier authorized gate; it never mechanically widens a private rule.
Existing N_LOOKUP_HIDDEN remains the more specific required write-target note;
avoid duplicate notes for that source site.

The rules card carries this lookup/refusal ladder and explicitly separates
program probes from rule probes. An executable packed-package qualification
runs every newly added/changed Quarry example as written and checks absent,
hidden, readable and expired rows plus statement precedence. Existing
SEC/SEC3 existence-oracle lints keep their source-level scope: a readable
row's custom later failure can intentionally reveal its existence, while
hidden and absent remain equivalent. SEC4 owns security-analysis changes.

## 2. A short common read

Wave-20 list presentation addition: LLP 3000.000.000.001 §10 defines the
packaged ReadState component; the query hooks below retain their contracts.

Add `useQueryData(op, args, options?)` in `snapback4/react`, shared by React
and Expo. It delegates directly to `useQuery` and returns `R | undefined`:
loading gives undefined; present, absent and partial give their exact data
(including null, empty lists, false and zero). A denied read throws
`QueryRefusal extends Error`, carrying the original typed `why: Refusal`.
An error boundary may render it; callers choosing inline refusal UI use
`useQueryResult`, which returns `{data: R | undefined, why: Refusal | null,
read: Read<R>}` without throwing. These hooks do not substitute an empty list for loading/refusal. They add
no cache, previous-argument retention or observation ownership. `read` is the same snapshot as `useQuery`.

A data-only read does not promise completeness or freshness. It is for
screens that show the authorized rows that arrived. Pagination, absence proofs,
and actions depending on fresh or complete results continue to use `useQuery`
or `usePage` and their metadata. The precise API remains unchanged. Skipping
uses the existing typed arguments and `{skip: true}`. Required/mistyped
arguments still fail typechecking; result types come from generated operations.
`useMutation(op).run` is already a typed callable and remains unchanged.

Add `<SignedIn fallback={...} restoring={...}>...</SignedIn>` inside
AppProvider (bare SnapbackProvider is insufficient), using the same
`useAuth()` snapshot as AppProvider. Signed-in children mount only in that
state; restoring defaults to null, signed-out uses fallback. The existing
AppProvider account boundary resets account-owned state. Children must be JSX
components (React elements), not eagerly invoked component functions.
No bundled login UI or new session runtime is added to the React entry.

### 7.2 Wave 3 (0.4.18): init first, schema second

Wave-20 custody amendment: LLP 3000.000.000.001 §10 keeps a runnable frontend
proof scaffold across adapt and moves Expo Metro/native smoke support into
the adapter package; edited application files remain owned by the app.

Wave 3 of the app farm (100 agents on 0.4.18) showed that §7.1's fixes fire
only when the schema exists *before* `init`. The README and the brief lead
agents to `init --web/--expo` first; they then replace `snapback/schema.q` and
are left with the todo starter's `fixtures/todos.jsonl` and cases (`test` runs
nothing), a guest sign-in screen over a persona-only schema (`auth.guest()`
refuses `E_AUTH`), or, rerunning init to get the picker, `E_INIT_CONFLICT`
(21 lanes, 41 minutes). The decisions, which make the outcome independent of
the order:

- **Leftovers are judged by the starter's bytes.** A starter file is a
  leftover only while it is byte-identical to what init wrote (the screen
  and client compared after normalizing the backend port and the persona
  list, the two values init varies) *and* it no longer fits the schema: the
  fixtures and cases when no `todos` table with `list`/`add`/`toggle`/`remove`
  exists; the screen and client when the schema's sign-in wants the other
  screen (guest for `use identity` with guests, the persona picker for
  `use personas` without `use identity`, or a picker for a different cast).
  A file the project changed is never reported as a leftover and never
  touched. No manifest is written: the starter text embedded in the binary is
  the reference, so a project that has never run 0.4.19's init still qualifies.
- **`check` names them, `init --adapt` fits them.** A successful `check`
  ends with a `starter:` block listing each leftover and its reason, then
  one command, `snapback4 init --adapt` (`check --json`: `starterLeftovers`
  with `files`, `advice` and `fix`). It never changes the exit status.
  `init --adapt [dir]` removes the unmodified fixtures (0.4.19 also removed
  an emptied `fixtures/`; §7.4 reverses that), and rewrites the unmodified screen and client to exactly
  what schema-first init writes for the same schema and port. A password-only
  or identity-less schema, and an adapted screen whose `Todos` component still
  calls the starter's operations, get advice lines rather than a rewrite.
  `--adapt` accepts only `--web`/`--expo` beside it and refuses without a
  `snapback/*.q`.
- **A project's `snapback/*.q` is never a conflict.** With any `.q` present,
  init leaves the starter's `schema.q` out with or without `--skip-existing`,
  lists the project's `.q` files as kept, and never writes through a linked
  schema. This replaces §7.1's "a conflict (or, with `--skip-existing`, kept
  out)". When an `E_INIT_CONFLICT` lists the files of an earlier starter that
  `--adapt` would fit, its first line and its rewrite name `init --adapt`.
- `test`'s refusal of a stray `todos.jsonl` names `init --adapt` as well.

Not done: `test` does not silently skip starter fixtures; a run that
executes nothing stays a refusal, and the command to fix it is one line.
(§7.4 skips the unmodified starter rows loudly instead.)

import { requireOptionalNativeModule } from "expo-modules-core";
import { createWitness, type Witness, type WitnessContainer } from "./witness-core";
export type { Witness } from "./witness-core";

import { witnessRuntime } from "./witness-runtime";

let instance: Witness | null | undefined;
/** Null on ordinary launches and outside an iOS simulator driven by `snapback4 witness ios`. */
export function witness(): Witness | null {
  if (instance === undefined) {
    const container = requireOptionalNativeModule<WitnessContainer>("Snapback4");
    instance = container?.witnessLaunch && JSON.parse(container.witnessLaunch).smoke === true ? null : createWitness(container, witnessRuntime());
  }
  return instance;
}

/** The starter may use normal guest sign-in during prime; never on ordinary launches. */
export function smokeSegment(): "prime" | "offline" | "restart" | null {
  const container = requireOptionalNativeModule<WitnessContainer>("Snapback4");
  if (!container?.witnessLaunch) return null;
  const config = JSON.parse(container.witnessLaunch);
  return config.smoke === true && ["prime", "offline", "restart"].includes(config.segment) ? config.segment : null;
}

/** Simulator smoke uses its owned loopback backend; ordinary launches keep the app URL. */
export function smokeOrigin(fallback: string): string {
  const container = requireOptionalNativeModule<WitnessContainer>("Snapback4");
  if (!container?.witnessLaunch) return fallback;
  const config = JSON.parse(container.witnessLaunch);
  return config.smoke === true && /^http:\/\/127\.0\.0\.1:[0-9]+$/.test(config.origin) ? config.origin : fallback;
}

/** Disposable account supplied only by the owned prime smoke launch. */
export function smokeAccount(): { email: string; password: string } | null {
  const container = requireOptionalNativeModule<WitnessContainer>("Snapback4");
  if (!container?.witnessLaunch) return null;
  const config = JSON.parse(container.witnessLaunch);
  return config.smoke === true && config.segment === "prime" && typeof config.smokeAccount?.email === "string" && typeof config.smokeAccount?.password === "string" ? config.smokeAccount : null;
}

# LLP 3000.000.000.001: Staging with real users

**Type:** RFC
**Status:** Implemented
**Systems:** Snapback 4 deployment, password identity, development doors, proof kit
**Author:** Codex for Charlie Cheever (STAGE)
**Date:** 2026-10-18
**Revised:** 2026-10-21 (DX5 §10); 2026-10-19 (DX4 §§8–9); 2026-10-18
**Related:** [Release activation](./3000.000.000-retained-storage-and-hot-release.rfc.md), [Proof kit](./3000.011.003.000.000-packaged-proof-kit.rfc.md), [Store ownership](./3000.019-what-the-builder-still-wrote.rfc.md#34-p8-residency-you-can-see-and-a-cli-that-does-not-fight-the-dev-server)

## 1. Commission and boundary

Implementer: STAGE, 2026-10-18, commissioned by Charlie's wave-16 bakeoff
fixes #1/#4. Ten Muse probes used dev because password-role provisioning
had no single recipe. This amendment supplies that recipe using the existing
signup and service-seat authority. No system seed door is added to serve.
SEC owns self-promotion lints and security invariants; KIT4 owns unrelated
proof helpers, PROD2 owns production starter adaptation.

`deploy <dir> --staging` classifies a **new deployment store**, under its
exclusive owner, with durable metadata `deployment_environment=staging`.
An existing store with no classification is production, including legacy stores;
it cannot be relabelled. A staging store remains staging through deploy,
rollback, restart, copying and source edits. There is no promote/relabel flag:
production requires a separate fresh deployment without --staging and real
operator provisioning. --check never creates the classification. Repeating
--staging on an already staging store is allowed, including while serve runs;
it verifies the existing classification without changing it. Malicious edits by
the filesystem/database owner are outside the threat model, as for service tokens.
This is a deployment-lifetime boundary stronger than a mutable per-release flag:
production source or a seed plan cannot opt a production store into test setup.

## 2. Real staging accounts

`GET /auth/config` reports `development` independently of door availability,
`devDoors`, and `environment` (`development`, `staging`, or `production`).
Missing/unknown environment metadata is production. serve remains bearer-only
in both environments, with the same password verifiers, session lifetimes,
rules, rate limits, clock and data plane. No password hashing or grant bypass.

`startServe(dir, options)` additionally returns `operatorToken(service =
"operator", days = 1)` and `seedAccounts(options)`. Minting uses the existing
local CLI proof protocol, captures secret stdout in memory and never writes
tokens into proof logs. It confers only that service seat's existing authority.
Tokens may also be requested on production for first-admin setup.

`seedAccounts({roles, provision, args?})` creates N real password accounts per
role, then calls the declared mutation as service:operator; `args(account)`
maps the account to application arguments (default `{principal, role}`).
`provision` is a generated mutation handle or `{name}`, including qualified names such as `accounts.provision`. The returned records
contain email, password, principal, token and expiresAt, grouped by role.
`startServe(dir, {seedUsers: options})` performs the same setup before returning
and exposes those records as `sessions`. Before minting or creating accounts,
the helper requires environment=staging and development=false. Production,
legacy and dev hosts refuse. Inputs are validated before effects; signup is
sequential, bounded, respects identity throttling, and never retries an ambiguous
write. A fresh call creates a fresh random email/password set. Partial failure
does not claim rollback: some accounts/grants may exist; discard the disposable
staging deployment or inspect it before retrying. Application data is created
through ordinary authenticated mutations after provisioning.

Credential records are returned to the operator, never logged by the helper.
The tested guide writes them to an exclusively created 0600 file. They must
not enter source control or reports. There is no public provisioning HTTP
endpoint beyond the application's declared rule-checked mutation.

## 3. First admin

The tested guide uses password signup (which grants no role), then the
filesystem owner's `operatorToken()` to invoke an operator-only mutation.
The roster's insert rule independently requires service:operator. No "first
caller wins", empty-roster bypass, client-selected signup role, or permanent
operator credential in the frontend. The same recipe works on production
with explicit operator-selected email/password; bulk seedAccounts refuses there.
Privileged account tokens cannot mint service tokens. SEC owns lints for
self-bootstrapped global authority; the guide points to this ownership.

## 4. Development doors

For password-only schemas (`auth.password && !auth.guests`), dev disables
`/seed`, every `/dev/*` door (except the existing cryptographically protected
local token protocol), and persona headers by default. The pre-existing serve
GET /dev/latency inspection remains service-authenticated; it never admits an
unauthenticated caller and its reset remains refused. `dev
--unsafe-dev-doors` is explicit opt-in with a prominent warning; serve accepts
no such flag. Host/Origin loopback fences still apply. Door availability is
computed from the current adopted schema, so hot adoption to password-only
also closes them. Seed/reset, clock advance and dev job enqueue revalidate
against the engine schema under the writer immediately before privileged effects;
slow request bodies and requests queued behind adoption cannot retain authority.
Action admission/replay, session-route admission, persona cancellation and upload
owner state transitions likewise revalidate under their actual writer. Previously
admitted durable work retains the existing work-record contract; a refused
new request creates no claimable work.
Persona reads also revalidate against the engine used to evaluate the query,
sync page or asset grant, checking the current declared cast at that read’s
admission. In-flight reads retain their existing snapshot semantics: cast
publication does not lock out concurrent ordinary writes, and the engine
transaction rejects a replaced execution schema.
Change-poll presence entry revalidates under its engine. A detached old
schema is fenced by the engine transaction; a replacement password-only reader
cannot inherit a pre-adoption persona capability. A persona header must name an explicitly declared persona;
an empty declaration admits none. Persona-based schemas retain their ordinary
development workflow. /auth/config always reports development=true on dev,
even with closed doors, so probe tooling can refuse it.

`startDev` follows native persistent storage by default, consuming the old
--no-memory alias; --memory/--fresh explicitly request disposable storage.
The returned now() refuses with guidance if the clock door is closed. Native
readiness plus the per-launch proof marker still establish host identity when
/dev/status is unavailable. Existing fixture/clock tests explicitly opt into
unsafe dev doors when their password schema requires those tools. Generated
frontend proofs explicitly select --memory and --unsafe-dev-doors, preserving
disposable fixture isolation and repeatability under the persistent helper
default. Exact 0.4.30/0.4.31 proof templates are retained and safely adapted
by digest; custom scripts remain untouched. DAY5 owns other starter custody.

## 5. Evidence

Required: production relabelling refusal before writes; staging retention over
hot/cold release switches; real signup/login per role and operator-only grants;
self-grant and unauthenticated doors refused; default/explicit dev doors and
schema-adoption closure; persistent/default and disposable dev; private token
logs; the exact guide recipe executed from the packed tarball in Linux
qualification, including production bulk-seed refusal and first admin; three
copied wave-16 dev probes converted to serve. Full crate tests, affected client
tests, Darwin affected tests on the assigned Mac Studio, ref-check, docs budget
and root inventory/guide checks. Never use the full scripts/test.sh here;
qualify-linux --consumer-only complements the manually run crate suites.

# LLP 3000.011.003.000.000: Packaged application proof kit

**Type:** RFC
**Status:** Implemented
**Systems:** Snapback 4 proof tooling, starters, fixtures, release source selection
**Author:** Codex for Charlie Cheever
**Date:** 2026-10-14
**Revised:** 2026-10-18 (DAY5 amendments; KIT4 clock, proof and test contracts); 2026-10-17 (KIT3 proof and clock contracts); 2026-10-16 (REG missing frontend export diagnostic; §11: wave-14 DAY4); 2026-10-16 (§9: wave-13 DAY3; §10: wave-13 KIT2); 2026-10-16 (§8: explicit platform boundary and client-source guard); 2026-10-15 (§8: wave-12 KIT and observational listener qualification)
**Related:** [Starters](./3000.011.003.000-offline-ready-application-starters.rfc.md), [Release activation](./3000.000.000-retained-storage-and-hot-release.rfc.md), [Built application proof](./3000.011.005.000-qualify-the-built-application.rfc.md)

STAGE staging and persistent startDev defaults are amended by [LLP 3000.000.000.001](./3000.000.000.001-staging-with-real-users.rfc.md); KIT4 owns other ongoing helper changes.

## 1. Contract

Implementer: PROOF workstream, 2026-10-14. Wave 11 fix list 1 authorizes
one published `snapback4/proof` Node module. It owns orchestration, never client
custody or backend/bundler supervision in the product. Existing `startDev(args)`
and `stopChild(child | {url, stop})` recipes remain usable as module exports.

`startDev`, `startServe(directory)`, `startStatic(directory)` and
`startVite(directory)` return `{url, pid, logs, stop}`. Options carry cwd,
environment, arguments and bounded ready/stop deadlines. Read PORT_LO/PORT_HI
at invocation: absent means an OS-assigned port; exactly one set refuses. With
both set, validate 1 <= LO <= HI <= 65535 and bind the first free port in that
inclusive range; exhaustion refuses. Qualification's occupied first port must
be skipped, never adopted. The existing native SNAPBACK4_READY line already names its direct child PID (LLP 3000.011.004.000); no new readiness log is needed. The listening process binds first and keeps that socket;
never adopt an already-serving port. Vite uses its supported JavaScript server
API in a directly spawned Node child, strict ports, the project's config and
a per-launch identity middleware. The directly spawned frontend calls its
server listen API for each candidate; no probe-and-release step exists. With
no range it calls listen on port 0, which the tested Vite API supports with
strictPort; it reads the actual retained socket address. Static hosting uses a directly spawned Node
child with traversal protection, correct wasm MIME and SPA fallback.

All child stdout/stderr go to separate files beneath `logs/`. Read complete
lines from those files, strip ANSI, bound readiness, and reject premature exit.
Native ready lines must name the directly spawned PID. To assert HTTP identity,
the kit sets a random SNAPBACK4_PROOF_ID only in the child environment;
`/auth/config` includes `proof_id` only when this variable is nonempty. It
confers no authority or bypass, and ordinary servers omit it. Both static and Vite frontend child
responses carry an `x-snapback4-proof` marker. Identity validation
precedes returning a handle. No public development door is enabled in serve.

Register every spawned child and browser process for an exit-time SIGKILL
sweep, using retained native ChildProcess handles, not process-name kills.
TERM followed by bounded KILL/reap stops a child. Every cleanup action has
its own bound and later actions still run when an earlier action fails.
`cli(args)` runs the native binary, awaits close, returns separate stdout and
stderr, and has a command deadline. It never runs npm/npx or shell strings.

`withBrowser({executablePath: process.env.CHROME}, callback)` launches Chromium
through playwright-core, closes with a bound, and registers its actual browser
process. Root needs --no-sandbox; other hosts first attempt a sandboxed launch
and retry without it only on recognized sandbox-unavailable diagnostics: "No usable sandbox", "Running as
root without --no-sandbox", "Failed to move to new namespace", "SUID sandbox",
"sandbox ... Operation not permitted", or "Failed to unshare ... Operation not
permitted". Unrelated failures never retry.
`waitForFresh` polls for nonempty changed text; `fillRN` clears and types real
keystrokes; `statusText` uses text selectors; `selectByValue` selects stable
option values. The browser executable is CHROME (when provided), undefined executablePath is omitted from launch options, then Playwright's
installed Chromium is used; an absent executable refuses at launch, with its path.
waitForFresh defaults to 30 seconds. Binary resolution is resolveBinary from
the same installed snapback4 package (override SNAPBACK4_BIN only for explicit
workspace tests); the opt-in identity requires CLI/client 0.4.28 or newer and
an older CLI omits proof_id and therefore fails the exact marker assertion; no inferred version comparison or success claim is made. cli(args) does not
invoke package managers; publication uses its existing guarded command runner.

None interprets an HTTP acknowledgement as rendered settlement.

use snapback4_lang::compile;
use snapback4_core::{Context, Engine, Value, value::object};

const TABLES: &str = "table funding:
  owner: principal
  limit: int
  expires: time ?
  unique owner
  read <- .owner = viewer
  expire at .expires
  online only
table work:
  n: int
  public
  update <- allow
  online only
";

fn checked(body: &str) -> snapback4_lang::Bound {
    let bound = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), format!("{TABLES}{body}"))]);
    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
    bound
}

#[test]
fn optional_private_side_reads_name_the_hiding_rule_and_null_consequence() {
    for body in [
        "mutation required(who: principal):\n  return funding[who] ! else NO\n",
        "mutation approve(who: principal):\n  row = funding[who]\n  require (row.limit ?? 0) > 1 else NEEDS_APPROVAL\n  return null\n",
        "fn threshold(who: principal): funding[who]\nmutation approve(who: principal):\n  return threshold(who)\n",
        "fn threshold(who: principal): funding[who]\nmutation approve(who: principal, other: principal):\n  x = who\n  require x = viewer else NO\n  x = other\n  return threshold(x)\n",
    ] {
        let bound = checked(body);
        let notes: Vec<_> = bound.notes.iter().filter(|note| note.code == "N_LOOKUP_FILTERED").collect();
        assert_eq!(notes.len(), 1, "{:?}", bound.notes);
        assert!(notes[0].message.contains("read <- .owner = viewer") && notes[0].message.contains("returns null"), "{}", notes[0]);
        assert_eq!(notes[0].site.file, "schema.q");
        assert!(notes[0].site.line > 0);
        assert!(notes[0].rewrite.contains("projection"));
    }
}

#[test]
fn otherwise_readable_expired_rows_are_absent_in_mutations_and_helper_assertions() {
    let bound = checked("fn need(who: principal): funding[who] ! else NOT_FOUND\nmutation required(who: principal):\n  row = need(who)\n  require row.limit > 1 else TOO_LOW\n  return row.limit\nmutation early(who: principal):\n  require false else FIRST\n  return need(who)\nmutation optional(who: principal):\n  return funding[who]\n");
    let mut engine = Engine::memory(bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap();
    engine.seed([("funding".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("expired".into())), ("owner", Value::Id("viewer".into())), ("limit", Value::Int(3)), ("expires", Value::Int(10))]))]).unwrap();
    let ctx = |now| Context::new("viewer", [("who".into(), Value::Id("viewer".into()))].into()).at(now);
    assert!(matches!(engine.mutate("required", None, ctx(1)).unwrap().state, snapback4_core::WriteState::Sent { .. }));
    let optional = engine.mutate("optional", None, ctx(20)).unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(optional.state, snapback4_core::WriteState::Sent { result: Value::Null, .. }));
    for (op, code) in [("required", "NOT_FOUND"), ("early", "FIRST")] {
        let result = engine.mutate(op, None, ctx(20)).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(result.state, snapback4_core::WriteState::Failed { ref why, .. } if why.code == code), "{result:?}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn optional_and_required_lookups_keep_hidden_absent_and_expired_equivalent() {
    let bound = checked("fn peek(who: principal): funding[who]\nquery optional(who: principal):\n  return peek(who)\nquery required(who: principal):\n  row = funding[who] ! else NOT_FOUND\n  require row.limit > 1 else TOO_LOW\n  return row.limit\n");
    let mut engine = Engine::memory(bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap();
    engine.seed([
        ("funding".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("a".into())), ("owner", Value::Id("hidden".into())), ("limit", Value::Int(3)), ("expires", Value::Null)])),
        ("funding".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("b".into())), ("owner", Value::Id("expired".into())), ("limit", Value::Int(3)), ("expires", Value::Int(10))])),
        ("funding".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("c".into())), ("owner", Value::Id("viewer".into())), ("limit", Value::Int(3)), ("expires", Value::Null)])),
    ]).unwrap();
    let mut refusals = Vec::new();
    let mut meters = Vec::new();
    for who in ["hidden", "missing", "expired"] {
        let viewer = if who == "expired" { "expired" } else { "viewer" };
        let ctx = || Context::new(viewer, [("who".into(), Value::Id(who.into()))].into()).at(20);
        let optional = engine.query("optional", ctx()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(optional.data, Value::Null);
        assert!(optional.complete);
        meters.push(optional.metered);
        refusals.push(engine.query("required", ctx()).unwrap_err());
    }
    assert!(refusals.iter().all(|refusal| refusal.code == "NOT_FOUND"));
    assert!(meters.iter().all(|meter| *meter == meters[0]), "{meters:?}");
    assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(&refusals[0]).unwrap(), serde_json::to_value(&refusals[1]).unwrap());
    assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(&refusals[0]).unwrap(), serde_json::to_value(&refusals[2]).unwrap());
    let visible = engine.query("required", Context::new("viewer", [("who".into(), Value::Id("viewer".into()))].into()).at(20)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(visible.data, Value::Int(3));
}

#!/usr/bin/env node
// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000#14 — resolve once, pin core and adapters to that same release.
import { upgradeWarnings } from './upgrade-warnings.js';
import { synopsis } from './cli-usage.js';
import { readFileSync, existsSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { previousVersion, installedVersion, acknowledgeVersion, compareVersions, installedHistory, runtimeChanges } from './release-changes.js';

let migrationWarnings = [];
async function run() {
  const args = process.argv.slice(2).flatMap(arg => arg.startsWith('--to=') ? ['--to', arg.slice(5)] : [arg]);
  if (args.length === 1 && args[0] === '--help') { console.log(`usage: ${synopsis('upgrade')}\nUpgrade snapback4 and every installed snapback4-expo adapter with npm, bun or pnpm; keep exact pins. Default: latest; refuses downgrades unless --to is explicit. Rebuild native apps after changing the adapter.`); return; }

import { Worker } from "node:worker_threads";

// The live keeper alone signals its own group. Closing its private pipe also
// cleans up if this runner dies; no cached PID ever authorizes a signal.
export async function runToolchainCommand(command, args, { cwd, env, timeout }) {
  const owner = fileURLToPath(new URL("./test-command-owner.mjs", import.meta.url));
  const keeper = spawn(process.execPath, [owner, "100", command, ...args], { cwd, env, detached: true, stdio: ["pipe", "inherit", "inherit", "ipc"] });
  let released = false, completed = false, failure, status;
  const release = mode => { if (!released) { released = true; keeper.stdin.end(mode); } };
  const fail = error => { failure ??= error; release("TERM"); };
  const timer = setTimeout(() => fail(Error(`${command}: toolchain command timed out`)), timeout);
  keeper.stdin.on("error", error => { failure ??= error; });
  keeper.on("message", message => {
    if (message.error) fail(Error(message.error));
    if (message.exited) { completed = true; status = message.status; release("KILL"); }
  });
  await new Promise(done => {
    keeper.once("error", error => { failure ??= error; });
    keeper.once("close", done);
  });
  clearTimeout(timer);
  if (!released || !completed) failure ??= Error(`${command}: command owner exited without a result`);
  // This read-only group-existence probe needs no /proc mount in the clean
  // userspace. Refuse on lingering members or ambiguous/permission errors.
  // Two empty observations also protect against a transient inspection result.
  const deadline = performance.now() + 5_000;
  let empty = 0;
  if (keeper.pid) while (empty < 2) {
    try { process.kill(-keeper.pid, 0); empty = 0; }
    catch (error) { if (error.code === "ESRCH") empty++; else { failure ??= error; break; } }
    if (empty === 2) break;
    if (performance.now() >= deadline) { failure ??= Error(`${command}: toolchain process group did not drain`); break; }
    await sleep(50);
  }
  if (failure) throw failure;
  if (status !== 0) throw Error(`${command}: toolchain command exited ${status}`);
}

async function boundedStop(work, label) {
  let timer;
  try { return await Promise.race([work, new Promise((_, reject) => { timer = setTimeout(() => reject(Error(label + " timed out")), 10_000); })]); }
  finally { clearTimeout(timer); }
}
export async function proveFrontendTwice(run, cwd, starter) {
  const results = [];
  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= 2; attempt++) {
    const occupied = createServer();
    const low = await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { occupied.once("error", reject); occupied.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", () => resolve(occupied.address().port)); });
    const high = Math.min(65535, low + 20);
    const workers = Array.from({ length: 2 }, () => new Worker(`setInterval(() => { const until = performance.now() + 25; while (performance.now() < until) {} }, 50);`, { eval: true }));
    const started = Date.now(), load = loadavg();
    const audit = join(cwd, `listener-audit-${attempt}.json`);
    const trace = join(cwd, `listener-audit-${attempt}.trace`);
    const auditEnabled = process.platform === "linux";
    const tracerVersion = auditEnabled ? (await import("./proof-listener-audit.mjs")).requireListenerTracer() : undefined;
    const proofLogs = join(cwd, `proof-logs-${attempt}`);
    try {
      rmSync(join(cwd, "dist"), { recursive: true, force: true });
      await run(auditEnabled ? "strace" : process.execPath, [...(auditEnabled ? ["-f", "-q", "-z", "-yy", "-e", "trace=listen", "-e", "signal=none", "-o", trace, process.execPath] : []), "scripts/frontend-proof.mjs"], cwd, { PORT_LO: String(low), PORT_HI: String(high), SNAPBACK4_PROOF_LOGS: proofLogs });
      const listenerAudit = auditEnabled ? (await import("./proof-listener-audit.mjs")).auditListenerTrace(readFileSync(trace, "utf8"), low, high) : { status: "not-run", reason: "listener audit belongs to Linux qualification" };
      if (auditEnabled) { assert.equal(listenerAudit.status, "passed"); assert.ok(listenerAudit.samples > 0); listenerAudit.tracerVersion = tracerVersion; }
      assert.ok(existsSync(proofLogs));
      writeFileSync(audit, JSON.stringify(listenerAudit));
      results.push({ starter: starter.id, kind: starter.kind, attempt, status: "passed", elapsedMs: Date.now() - started, range: [low, high], occupied: low, cpuLoadWorkers: workers.length, loadavg: load, listenerAudit, logs: proofLogs });
    } finally {
      const stopped = await Promise.allSettled([...workers.map(worker => boundedStop(worker.terminate(), "CPU worker stop")), boundedStop(new Promise(resolve => occupied.close(resolve)), "occupied listener close")]);
      const failures = stopped.filter(result => result.status === "rejected").map(result => result.reason);
      if (failures.length) throw new AggregateError(failures, "loaded-host proof cleanup failed");
    }
  }
  return results;
}

            for schedule in held.iter().filter(|s| s["holdCode"] == "saved-boundary") {
                eprintln!("clock: schedule {}: {}", schedule["name"].as_str().unwrap_or("?"), schedule["reason"].as_str().unwrap_or("held"));
            }
        }
        if let Some(denied) = json.get("denied") {
            let clock = json["message"].as_str().map(|message| format!("; time remains advanced: {message}")).unwrap_or_default();
            return Err(format!("{}: {}{clock}\n  guide: clock", denied["code"].as_str().unwrap_or("E_CLOCK_INPUT"), denied["message"].as_str().unwrap_or("clock advance failed")));
        }
        if status != 200 { return Err(format!("dev refused clock advance: {json}")); }
        Ok(json.to_string())
    })();
    match result { Ok(body) => { println!("{body}"); 0 }, Err(error) => { eprintln!("{error}"); 1 } }
}

    /// One atomic schedule boundary, so the host can release its writer between
    /// schedules. A changed/shortened schema is revisited on the next tick.
    pub fn fire_schedule_at(&mut self, now: i64, index: usize) -> Result<Vec<String>, RuntimeError> {
        self.fire_schedule_range(now, index..index.saturating_add(1), None)
    }

    /// Admit one historical period on the current clock. In particular an
    /// action's deadline begins at admission, not at the historical boundary.
    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.12.1 — period identity and admission time are distinct during explicit catch-up.
    pub fn fire_schedule_boundary_at(&mut self, now: i64, index: usize, boundary: i64) -> Result<Vec<String>, RuntimeError> {
        let schedule = self.schema.schedules.get(index).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input("unknown schedule index".into()))?;
        if schedule.boundary(boundary) != boundary || boundary > schedule.boundary(now) {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Input("schedule window must end at an elapsed boundary".into()));
        }
        self.fire_schedule_range(now, index..index.saturating_add(1), Some(boundary))
    }

    fn fire_schedule_range(&mut self, now: i64, range: std::ops::Range<usize>, selected: Option<i64>) -> Result<Vec<String>, RuntimeError> {
        let mut fired = Vec::new();
        for schedule in self.schema.schedules.get(range).unwrap_or(&[]).to_vec() {
            let boundary = selected.unwrap_or_else(|| schedule.boundary(now));
            let shape = digest(&schedule);
            let program = self.programs.get(&schedule.target).filter(|p| matches!(p.kind, ProgramKind::Job | ProgramKind::Action))
                .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("schedule {} names missing job or action {}; restore its target before firing it", schedule.name, schedule.target)))?.clone();
            if program.kind == ProgramKind::Action && !schedule.service.as_deref().is_some_and(crate::identity::is_service) {
                return Err(RuntimeError::Schema("a scheduled action requires its declared service seat".into()));
            }
            if program.kind == ProgramKind::Job && schedule.service.is_some() {
                return Err(RuntimeError::Schema("a scheduled job runs as the system, not a service seat".into()));
            }
            let tx = self.store.transaction()?;
            let previous_shape: Option<String> = tx.schedule_shape(&schedule.name)?;
            if previous_shape.as_ref().is_some_and(|previous| previous != &shape) {
                tx.set_schedule_boundary(&schedule.name, boundary)?;
                tx.set_schedule_shape(&schedule.name, &shape)?;
                tx.commit()?;
                continue;
            }
            tx.set_schedule_shape(&schedule.name, &shape)?;
            let last: Option<i64> = tx.schedule_boundary(&schedule.name)?;
            if last.is_some_and(|last| last >= boundary) {
                tx.commit()?;
                continue;
            }
            let Some(_) = last else {
                tx.set_schedule_boundary(&schedule.name, boundary)?;
                tx.commit()?;
                continue;
            };
            let mut args = BTreeMap::new();
            if program.args.contains_key("periodStart") {
                args.insert("periodStart".to_owned(), Value::Int(schedule.previous(boundary)));
            }
            if program.args.contains_key("periodEnd") {
                args.insert("periodEnd".to_owned(), Value::Int(boundary));
            }
            let id = crate::ids::mint(now, &mut self.minter)?;
            if program.kind == ProgramKind::Action {
                let principal = schedule.service.as_deref().expect("checked service seat");
                validate_inputs(&self.schema, &program, &mut args)?;
                super::actions::authorize(&program, principal)?;
                let raw = serde_json::Value::Object(crate::wire::map_to_json(&args));
                let context = Context::new(principal, args).at(now);
                // @ref LLP 3000.009#5.2 — the boundary and service-seat admission are one commit.
                super::actions::insert_request(&tx, &self.schema, &program, &id, &context, &raw, true, now)?;
            } else {
                #[cfg(feature = "native")]
                let program_hash = job_admission_hash(&program, self.native.as_deref().map(super::native::Module::digest));
                #[cfg(not(feature = "native"))]
                let program_hash = job_admission_hash(&program, None);
                tx.insert_job(&id, &schedule.target, &args, &program_hash, now)?;
            }
            tx.set_schedule_boundary(&schedule.name, boundary)?;
            tx.commit()?;
            fired.push(schedule.name.clone());
        }
        Ok(fired)
    }
}

//! Bounded, read-only evidence from the store's own commit clock.
use snapback4_core::{Engine, RuntimeError};
use std::collections::BTreeSet;

const SKIPPED_PREVIEW: usize = 32;
const TOLERANCE_MS: i64 = 5_000;
const RECENT_COMMITS: usize = 64;
const TABLE_BYTES: usize = 4096;
const TABLE_NAMES: usize = 8;
const REPORT_ERROR_BYTES: usize = 1024;
// Reserve one MiB for the outer clock/work envelope inside the host encoder.
// The reply retains `schedules` and its fired/held partition.
const REPORT_BYTE_BUDGET: usize = (crate::serve::JSON_RESPONSE_CEILING - (1 << 20)) / 2;

// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.12 — inspect a fixed recent commit window, never application row values.
pub fn ahead(engine: &Engine, now: i64) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError> {
    // Reverse primary-key traversal: no full scan, sort, row payloads or retained
    // historical stamp set. octet_length(column) uses SQLite record metadata;
    // unlike a text length/cast/substr, it need not load oversized payloads.
    let mut lead = 0;
    let mut tables = BTreeSet::new();
    let mut omitted = false;
    engine.store().visit_recent_commit_clock(now.saturating_add(TOLERANCE_MS), TABLE_BYTES as i64, RECENT_COMMITS as i64, |record| {
        let at = record.at;
        if at <= now.saturating_add(TOLERANCE_MS) { return Ok(()); }
        lead = lead.max(at.saturating_sub(now));
        let length = record.length.unwrap();
        if length > TABLE_BYTES as i64 { omitted = true; return Ok(()); }
        let bytes = record.touched.unwrap();
        match serde_json::from_slice::<Vec<String>>(&bytes) {
            Ok(names) => for name in names {
                if tables.contains(&name) { continue; }
                if tables.len() < TABLE_NAMES && name.len() <= 128 { tables.insert(name); }
                else { omitted = true; }
            },
            Err(_) => omitted = true,
        }
        Ok(())
    })?;
    if lead == 0 { return Ok(None); }
    let mut names = tables.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
    if omitted { names.push("additional tables omitted".into()); }
    if names.is_empty() { names.push("no table names recorded".into()); }
    Ok(Some(format!(
        "N_CLOCK_STORE_AHEAD: recent commit stamps lead the current clock by up to {lead}ms (latest {RECENT_COMMITS} commits; tables: {}); use a fresh store per offset test ({}), or restart with the same --clock-offset (or dev --resume-clock) to continue",
        names.join(", "), crate::dev_clock::isolated_command())))
}

/// UTC calendar text for Unix milliseconds: schedule boundaries are UTC.
pub fn utc(ms: i64) -> String {
    let (days, rem) = (ms.div_euclid(86_400_000), ms.rem_euclid(86_400_000));
    // Civil-from-days (proleptic Gregorian), exact for the I53 range.
    let z = days + 719_468;
    let era = z.div_euclid(146_097);
    let doe = z - era * 146_097;
    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1_460 + doe / 36_524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
    let day = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1;
    let month = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 };
    let year = yoe + era * 400 + i64::from(month <= 2);
    format!("{year:04}-{month:02}-{day:02}T{:02}:{:02}:{:02}Z", rem / 3_600_000, rem % 3_600_000 / 60_000, rem % 60_000 / 1_000)
}

// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000#8 — password identity gets an executable sign-in screen.
pub(super) fn identity_screens(platform: Platform, personas: Option<&[String]>, body: &Body, password: bool) -> (String, String) {
    let (app, client) = wave20_screens(platform, personas, body, password);
    let app = if platform == Platform::Expo { app.replace("import { useNativeSmokeGuest } from \"./src/native-smoke\";", "import { useNativeSmoke } from \"snapback4-expo/native-smoke\";")
        .replace("useNativeSmokeGuest();", if password { "useNativeSmoke(true);" } else { "useNativeSmoke();" }) } else { app };
    (app, client)
}
pub(super) fn wave20_screens(platform: Platform, personas: Option<&[String]>, body: &Body, password: bool) -> (String, String) { identity_screens_version(platform, personas, body, password, false) }
// Recognize only complete known templates; edited application source never matches.

fn identity_screens_version(platform: Platform, personas: Option<&[String]>, body: &Body, password: bool, previous: bool) -> (String, String) {
    let version = |current, old| if previous { old } else { current };
    if !password { return screens_version(platform, personas, body, previous); }
    let head = match platform { Platform::Web => include_str!("starter/web/password.tsx"), Platform::Expo => version(include_str!("starter/expo/password.tsx"), include_str!("starter/previous/wave9/expo-password.tsx")) };
    let (_, client) = screens_version(platform, None, body, previous);
    let body_source = match (platform, body) {
        (Platform::Web, Body::Todos) => version(include_str!("starter/web/todos.tsx"), include_str!("starter/previous/wave9/web-todos.tsx")).to_owned(),
        (Platform::Expo, Body::Todos) => version(include_str!("starter/expo/todos.tsx"), include_str!("starter/previous/wave9/expo-todos.tsx")).to_owned(),
        (platform, Body::Home(op)) => {
            let (home, first) = match platform { Platform::Web => (include_str!("starter/web/home.tsx"), include_str!("starter/web/first-read.tsx")), Platform::Expo => (include_str!("starter/expo/home.tsx"), include_str!("starter/expo/first-read.tsx")) };
            match op { Some(op) => compose(home, &first.replace("api.OP", &format!("api.{op}"))), None => home.replace("    <FirstRead />\n", "") }
        }
    };
    (compose(&head.replace("<Todos />", if matches!(body, Body::Todos) { "<Todos />" } else { "<Home />" }), &body_source), client)
}

pub(super) fn identity_readme(platform: Platform, title: &str, body: &Body, personas: bool, offline: &Offline, password: bool) -> String {
    let mut text = readme(platform, title, body, personas, offline);
    if platform == Platform::Expo && matches!(offline, Offline::Tables { synced, .. } if synced.is_empty()) {
        text = text.replace("web uses the wasm\ndevice", "web uses the principal write journal (no synced tables)")
            .replace("web uses the wasm device", "web uses the principal write journal (no synced tables)")
            .replace("web uses the\nwasm device", "web uses the principal write journal (no synced tables)")
            .replace("or `webDevice()` (web)", "or the principal write journal (web, no synced tables)");
    }
    let text = if password { text.replace(GUEST_SIGN_IN, "Sign up or sign in with email and password (`use identity password`); the SDK\nkeeps your session across restarts. See `snapback4 guide client --section password`.")
        .replace("Choose \"Continue as a guest\", then add", "Sign up or sign in with email and password, then add")
        .replace("Choose \"Continue as a\nguest\", then add", "Sign up or sign in with email and password, then add") } else { text };
    super::proof::readme(text)
}

/// Wave 14's previous exact screen bytes remain recognizable after the
/// improved complete-empty/denied rendering. Edited screens never match.
pub(super) fn wave14_screens(platform: Platform, personas: Option<&[String]>, body: &Body, password: bool) -> (String, String) {
    let (app, client) = wave20_screens(platform, personas, body, password);
    let (current, previous) = match platform {
        Platform::Web => (include_str!("starter/web/todos.tsx"), include_str!("starter/previous/wave14/web-todos.tsx")),
        Platform::Expo => (include_str!("starter/expo/todos.tsx"), include_str!("starter/previous/wave14/expo-todos.tsx")),
    };
    let (_, current_body) = current.split_once("\n\n").expect("imports end");
    let (_, previous_body) = previous.split_once("\n\n").expect("imports end");
    // Imports are coalesced by compose; the new isAbsent import is the sole
    // import delta between these two complete historical templates.
    (app.replace(current_body.trim(), previous_body.trim()).replace("isAbsent, isDenied", "isDenied"), client)
}

function Account() {
  useNativeSmokeGuest();
  const auth = useAuth();
  const ready = useAppReady();
  const [email, setEmail] = useState(""), [password, setPassword] = useState(""), [problem, setProblem] = useState(""), [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  if (auth.state === "restoring") return <Text>Restoring your session…</Text>;
  if (auth.state === "signed-in" && !ready) return <Text>{auth.why?.message ?? "Opening…"}</Text>;
  if (auth.state === "signed-in") return <Todos />;
  async function submit(signup: boolean) {
    setBusy(true); setProblem("");
    try { const result = await (signup ? auth.signup(email, password) : auth.login(email, password)); if (!result.ok) setProblem(result.why.message); }
    catch { setProblem("Sign-in failed; retry."); } finally { setBusy(false); }
  }
  return <View style={{ padding: 24, gap: 12 }}><Text>Sign in</Text>
    <TextInput accessibilityLabel="Email" autoCapitalize="none" autoComplete="email" keyboardType="email-address" value={email} onChangeText={setEmail} />
    <TextInput accessibilityLabel="Password" secureTextEntry autoComplete="current-password" value={password} onChangeText={setPassword} />
    <Button title="Sign in" disabled={busy} onPress={() => void submit(false)} /><Button title="Sign up" disabled={busy} onPress={() => void submit(true)} />
    <Text accessibilityRole="alert">{problem || auth.why?.message}</Text>
  </View>;
}

pub(super) fn without_offline(text: &str) -> String {
    let legacy = [
        ("the Snapback 4 web starter. It works offline and syncs when the link returns.\n", "the Snapback 4 web starter.\n\nOFFLINE\n"),
        ("started from the Snapback 4 Expo starter. Development and production builds\nopen the native device and work offline; Expo Go uses the online client; web\nuses the wasm device.\n",
            "started from the Snapback 4 Expo starter. Development and production builds\nopen the native device; Expo Go uses the online client; web uses the wasm\ndevice.\n\nOFFLINE\n"),
    ];
    let mut text = super::proof::without_readme(text).to_owned();
    // Recognize the exact previous quick-start command while moving generated
    // READMEs onto launchers. Application prose still participates byte-for-byte.
    text = text.split_inclusive('\n').map(|line| {
        let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix("npx snapback4 dev") else { return line.to_owned(); };
        let rest = if let Some(rest) = rest.strip_prefix(" --port ") {
            let digits = rest.chars().take_while(char::is_ascii_digit).count();
            if digits == 0 { return line.to_owned(); } else { &rest[digits..] }
        } else { rest };
        if rest.starts_with("        # serves ") { format!("npm run backend         # serves {}", rest.strip_prefix("        # serves ").unwrap()) } else { line.to_owned() }
    }).collect();

    for (old, new) in legacy { text = text.replacen(old, new, 1); }
    text = text.replace("web uses the principal write journal (no synced tables)", "web uses the wasm\ndevice")
        .replace("or the principal write journal (web, no synced tables)", "or `webDevice()` (web)")
        .replace("native device and work offline;", "native device;")
        .replace("web uses the wasm\ndevice", "web uses the wasm device")
        .replace("web uses the\nwasm device", "web uses the wasm device");
    let mut masked = text.split("\n\n").map(|paragraph| if paragraph.starts_with("Offline") { "OFFLINE" } else { paragraph }).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\n\n");
    if masked.starts_with("# Todos") && !masked.contains("\n\nOFFLINE\n\n") {
        masked = masked.replacen("wasm device.\n\n", "wasm device.\n\nOFFLINE\n\n", 1);
    }
    masked
}

pub(super) enum Platform { Web, Expo }

impl Platform {
    /// Where the starter writes its screen and its client.
    pub(super) fn paths(self) -> (&'static str, &'static str) {
        match self { Platform::Web => ("src/App.tsx", "src/client.ts"), Platform::Expo => ("App.tsx", "src/client.ts") }
    }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000#7.4 — wave 6 (042): adapt rewrote the screen but left a README about todos and guest sign-in.
fn readme(dir: &Path, own: &OwnSchema, todos: bool, found: &mut Vec<Leftover>, modified: &mut Vec<String>) {
    let platform = if dir.join("src/App.tsx").is_file() { Platform::Web } else if dir.join("App.tsx").is_file() { Platform::Expo } else { return };
    let title = super::title(dir);
    let personas = own.identity.is_none() && !own.personas.is_empty();
    let wanted_body = if todos { Body::Todos } else { Body::Home(None) };
    for path in ["README.md", "README.snapback.md"] {
        let Some(text) = read(dir, path) else { continue };
        let port = number_after(&text, "127.0.0.1:");
        let web_port = number_after(&text, "localhost:");
        let ports = [(port, web_port), (None, web_port), (port, None), (None, None)];
        // The offline paragraph names the schema's synced tables when init
        // wrote it; any of them (or 0.4.22's unconditional claim) still matches.
        let masked = starter::without_offline(&text);
        let explicit_online = platform == Platform::Web && read(dir, "src/client.ts").is_some_and(|client| client.contains("writes: \"online\""));
        let matched = ports.into_iter().find(|&(port, web_port)| {
            [(Body::Todos, false), (Body::Home(None), false), (Body::Home(None), true)].iter()
                .any(|(body, personas)| [false, true].iter().any(|password| [false, true].iter().any(|online| {
                    let readme = starter::identity_readme(platform, &title, body, *personas, &starter::Offline::Unknown, *password);
                    let readme = if *online { starter::online_readme(&readme) } else { readme };
                    masked == starter::without_offline(&super::localize(path, &super::without_design_references(&readme), port, web_port))
                })))
        });
        let Some((port, web_port)) = matched else { modified.push(path.to_owned()); continue };
        let wanted = super::localize(path, &super::without_design_references(&starter::identity_readme(platform, &title, &wanted_body, personas, &own.offline, own.identity.is_some_and(|(password, guests)| password && !guests))), port, web_port);
        let wanted = if explicit_online { starter::online_readme(&wanted) } else { wanted };
        let wanted = if todos { super::proof::readme(wanted) } else { wanted };
        if wanted == text { continue; }
        let about = if todos { "the todo starter's operations, which your snapback/*.q declares again" } else { "your snapback/*.q and the Home screen, named after this directory" };
        let only_proof = super::proof::without_readme(&wanted) == text;
        let only_offline = !text.starts_with("# Todos") && starter::without_offline(&wanted) == masked;
        // A schema that does not compile right now says nothing about what it syncs.
        if only_offline && !only_proof && own.offline == starter::Offline::Unknown { continue; }
        let why = if only_proof {
            "the unmodified starter README lacks frontend/day-two proof instructions; adapt adds them".to_owned()
        } else if only_offline {
            "the unmodified starter README says what works offline for another schema; adapt rewrites that paragraph from the tables your snapback/*.q syncs".to_owned()
        } else {
            format!("the unmodified starter README describes {}; adapt rewrites it to describe {about}", if text.starts_with("# Todos") { "the todo starter (its todos table and guest sign-in)" } else { "the Home screen for another schema" })
        };
        found.push(Leftover { path, why, rewrite: Some(wanted) });
    }
}

#[test]
fn generated_proofs_read_ports_at_execution_and_declare_the_driver() {
    for flag in ["--web", "--expo"] {
        let dir = Dir::new();
        let output = Command::new(BIN).args(["init", flag]).env("PORT_LO", "29040").env("PORT_HI", "29049").current_dir(&dir.0).output().unwrap();
        assert!(output.status.success(), "{output:?}");
        let package: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(dir.0.join("package.json")).unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(package["scripts"]["frontend:proof"], "node scripts/frontend-proof.mjs");
        assert_eq!(package["devDependencies"]["playwright-core"], "1.55.1");
        for path in ["package.json", "scripts/frontend-proof.mjs"] {
            let body = fs::read_to_string(dir.0.join(path)).unwrap();
            assert!(!body.contains("29040") && !body.contains("29041") && !body.contains("29049"), "{flag}: initializer's environment leaked into {path}");
        }
        assert!(fs::read_to_string(dir.0.join("scripts/launch.mjs")).unwrap().contains("low === null ? 29040"));
        assert!(fs::read_to_string(dir.0.join("src/client.ts")).unwrap().contains("http://127.0.0.1:29040"));
        let proof = fs::read_to_string(dir.0.join("scripts/frontend-proof.mjs")).unwrap();
        assert!(proof.contains("snapback4/proof") && proof.contains("encodeURIComponent(dev.url)") && proof.contains("cleanup("));
        assert!(!proof.contains("spawn(") && !proof.contains("npx") && !proof.contains("--port"));
    }
}

#[test]
fn adapt_adds_missing_proof_files_and_preserves_application_proofs() {
    let dir = Dir::new(); assert!(dir.run("--web").status.success());
    fs::remove_dir_all(dir.0.join("scripts")).unwrap();
    let path = dir.0.join("package.json");
    let mut package: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(&path).unwrap()).unwrap();
    // The missing proof is still referenced by frontend:proof.

    package["devDependencies"].as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("playwright-core");
    fs::write(&path, package.to_string()).unwrap();
    assert!(dir.init(&["--adapt", "--apply"]).status.success());
    assert!(dir.0.join("scripts/frontend-proof.mjs").is_file());
    let mut package: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(&path).unwrap()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(package["scripts"]["frontend:proof"], "node scripts/frontend-proof.mjs");
    assert_eq!(package["devDependencies"]["playwright-core"], "1.55.1");
    package["scripts"]["frontend:proof"] = json!("my-custom-proof"); fs::write(&path, package.to_string()).unwrap();
    fs::write(dir.0.join("scripts/frontend-proof.mjs"), "// application-owned proof\n").unwrap();
    assert!(dir.init(&["--adapt", "--apply"]).status.success());
    let package: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(&path).unwrap()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(package["scripts"]["frontend:proof"], "my-custom-proof");
    assert_eq!(fs::read_to_string(dir.0.join("scripts/frontend-proof.mjs")).unwrap(), "// application-owned proof\n");
}

pub(super) fn legacy_differences(dir: &Path, plan: &[(&str, String)]) -> Vec<String> {

            for entry in entries.flatten() {
                let path = entry.path();
                if path.extension().is_some_and(|ext|ext=="q") && let Ok(text)=std::fs::read_to_string(&path) {
                    saved.insert(format!("{prefix}{}",entry.file_name().to_string_lossy()),text);
                }
            }
        }
        for (name,text) in plan.iter().filter(|(name,_)|name.starts_with(&prefix) && name.ends_with(".q")) {
            saved.insert((*name).to_owned(),text.clone());
        }
        if saved.is_empty() || saved.len()==1 && saved.values().next()==Some(&legacy) {return None;}
        let paths=saved.keys().cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
        Some(format!("info: {flat} differs from {paths}; saved {version} captures snapback/*.q, not the legacy flat source; both remain unchanged evidence. Review the pair before day2:proof"))
    }).collect()
}

export async function proveStarters(client, platform, expo, directory, browserProofs = true) {

  delete env.SNAPBACK4_BIN;
  const deadline = performance.now() + 1_200_000;
  const run = (cmd, args, cwd, overrides = {}) => {
    const remaining = Math.ceil(deadline - performance.now());
    if (remaining <= 0) throw Error("starter qualification exceeded its twenty-minute guard");
    return runToolchainCommand(cmd, args, { cwd, env: { ...env, ...overrides }, timeout: Math.min(300_000, remaining) });
  };
  const artifacts = [client, platform, expo].map(path => resolve(path));

    writeFileSync(join(cwd, "package.json"), '{"private":true}');
    // Install the CLI first so init and all later package scripts resolve the
    // packed binary. Pin native JS in init's manifest before dependency install.
    await run("npm", ["install", "--no-save", "--ignore-scripts", "--no-audit", "--no-fund", ...artifacts.slice(0, 2)], cwd);
    const cli = join(cwd, "node_modules/.bin/snapback4");
    await run(cli, ["init", ...flags], cwd);
    const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(cwd, "package.json")));
    pkg.dependencies.snapback4 = `file:${artifacts[0]}`;
    pkg.optionalDependencies = { [`snapback4-${process.platform}-${process.arch}`]: `file:${artifacts[1]}` };
    if (kind === "expo") pkg.dependencies["snapback4-expo"] = `file:${artifacts[2]}`;
    writeFileSync(join(cwd, "package.json"), JSON.stringify(pkg, null, 2));
    // Lifecycle scripts are enabled: esbuild and the other real tools need them.
    await run("npm", ["install", "--prefer-offline", "--no-audit", "--no-fund"], cwd);

## 12. Wave 15 proof diagnostics and clock sampling (KIT4)

Implementer: Codex, 2026-10-18, commissioned for 0.4.32. On a canonical
argument mismatch the shared E_WITNESS_UNCLAIMED message names the differing
top-level keys. withBrowser installs a diagnostic binding which writes the
full armed and actual arguments to a fresh mode-0600 *.witness.private.jsonl
file under the proof log directory. Receipt messages contain no argument values.
Diagnostic failure never cancels, retries or blocks the application's write.
This supersedes §11's suppression of argument values in all retained logs;
private proof logs intentionally contain sensitive application evidence.

Substring timeout advice requires an explicitly scoped renderedText or
waitForFresh locator and a substring within that scope. Whole-page prose
cannot trigger the hint. A timeout includes up to three visible page headings

codex
I found a stale consumer of the changed clock API: the packed staging proof still subtracts the `{now, fired, held}` object from a timestamp. That yields `NaN`, so the assertion always fails after a successful advance. I’m checking the remaining call sites before finishing the verdict.

+/** Render a list read or page in one expression. Empty describes returned
+ * rows, including partial/stale answers; it never proves absence. This owns
+ * no observation and does not retain a previous read. Native callers supply
+ * Text/View elements in the same slots. A missing denied renderer throws the
+ * original typed QueryRefusal for an error boundary. */
+// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#10-wave-20-loop-repairs-dx5 — presentation preserves precise read evidence.
+export function ReadState<R extends readonly unknown[]>({ read: source, loading = null, empty = null, denied, children }: {
+  read: Read<R> | { read: Read<R> };
+  loading?: ReactNode;
+  empty?: ReactNode;
+  denied?: (why: Refusal) => ReactNode;
+  children: (items: R, read: Ready<R>) => ReactNode;
+}): ReactNode {
+  const read = "read" in source ? source.read : source;
+  if ("denied" in read) {
+    if (denied) return denied(read.denied);
+    throw new QueryRefusal(read.denied);
+  }
+  if (!("data" in read)) return loading;
+  return read.data.length === 0 ? empty : children(read.data, read);

## Local fixture tools are explicit

Password-only dev closes /seed, /dev/* and persona headers by default.
`dev --unsafe-dev-doors` explicitly opens local fixture and clock tools and
prints a warning; it still requires loopback Host/Origin, and personas must be
declared with `use personas`. The local token-mint protocol keeps its existing
private store-owner proof. Serve never opens these development tools.
`/auth/config` reports `environment`, `development`, and `devDoors` separately.
`startDev()` persists by default, matching native dev; pass args:["--memory"]
for disposable storage. now() needs the explicit clock door on password-only
dev. A proof for real users uses the serve recipe above.

## Time and reused stores

`await host.advance("49h")` returns `{now, fired, held}`; `await host.now()` still
returns a timestamp. The CLI `clock advance 49h --release staging` returns the
same outcomes. Fired means enqueued, so inspect each run state for parked work.
Every held schedule gives a reason and next boundary. Saved boundaries survive
restart: each boundary fires once; missed periods coalesce unless eachBoundary
is explicit. A reused store can hold a due application row because that window
already ran. The helper and CLI print the saved-boundary hold and recovery on
stderr. Advance beyond the saved boundary's next window, keep --clock-offset
across serve restarts when continuing, or deploy a fresh staging directory for
an independent test. Never replay a lost advance reply. Time travel also ages
sessions and unplaced uploads: log in again and upload bytes after a large jump.

- **2026-09-12 — operation names (lead).** Operations in `schema.q` are bare
  (`api.thread`); operations in `snapback/<module>.q` are `<module>.<name>`
  (`api.feed.home`). Generated types are built into
  `snapback/generated/api.ts` by `check` and `dev`, never committed.

- **2026-09-12 — delivery is bound to the rule's probe (lead, after the
  partition review).** `sync to target[.prefix]` is sound only when the
  table's read rule is exactly `exists target[.prefix, viewer]` (a second
  disjunct or a conjunct is refused with the rewrite) and the audience
  index is unique; the partition log delivers by that probe's index and
  never by a mapping reconstructed from column names or types; principal
  partitions are tagged so no principal's name collides with `public`; a
  commit is delivered whole however large; a grant that ends inside its
  own commit delivers nothing; a delivered aggregate's audience is its
  source's. Horizons bound acquisition, not holdings: a device holds what
  was delivered, and a local read past the horizon says `complete: false`.
- **2026-09-12 — completeness is a class, not a count (lead, after the
  meter review).** As Snapback 2 (LLP 1001 §3): a query with a scan the
  prefix does not decide is `complete: false` whatever the meter found,
  and a capped page's `next` continues from its last visible row or ends
  on an empty page; the meter's numbers, its cut site and a refusal's
  count stay off the viewer wire; a hidden row costs what a miss costs and
  a hoisted-false range what an empty one costs. The device runs the same
  hoist; its `complete` speaks of the horizon and the meter alone, since a
  device holds only its partition.

  **2026-09-15 — W7c development inspection (author's lane brief).**
  Loopback `dev` may return the existing engine counters on successful reads
  explicitly requesting `x-snapback-meter: 1`; the online client exposes this
