/** A query `usePage` can page: it takes its cursor as `c` (`c: cursor ?` in
 * the schema) and reads `after c`. Any other query names the fix in its error. */
type PagedQuery<A, R> = Query<A, R> & ("c" extends keyof A ? unknown
  : { readonly "usePage needs a query that declares `c: cursor ?` and reads `after c`; see `snapback4 guide reads`": true });

/** Own the current requested cursor chain. A changed/withdrawn cursor releases
 * its old suffix. Mount this hook in an active route child; keep the composer
 * outside that child and bound point-reader IDs to requested pages/visible rows.
 * See the bounded screen recipe in CLIENT-AND-OPERATIONS.md.
 */
export function usePage<A, R extends readonly unknown[]>(op: PagedQuery<A, R>, args: Omit<A, "c">, options?: ReadHookOptions): PageHook<R> {
  const client = useClient();
  const skip = options?.skip === true;
  const key = skip ? null : readKey(op, args);
  const paged = op as Query<A & { c?: Cursor | null }, R>;
  const pages = useMemo(() => skip ? SKIPPED_PAGES : new Pages(client, paged, args as A & { c?: Cursor | null }, observeOptions(options)), [client, op, key, options?.keep, skip]); // eslint-disable-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  const snapshot = useSyncExternalStore(pages.subscribe, pages.getSnapshot, pages.getSnapshot);
  return { items: snapshot.items as R[number][], hasMore: snapshot.hasMore, read: snapshot.read as Read<R>, loadMore: pages.loadMore };
}
/** The page chain a skipped `usePage` holds: loading, no items, nothing to load. */
const SKIPPED_PAGE_SNAPSHOT = { items: [] as never[], hasMore: false, read: LOADING };
const SKIPPED_PAGES = { subscribe: () => () => {}, getSnapshot: () => SKIPPED_PAGE_SNAPSHOT, loadMore: () => {} };

/** Complete online Following history; the SDK owns preparation and replay. */
export function useFollowing<A, R extends readonly unknown[]>(op: FollowingQuery<A, R>, args: A) {
  const client = useClient(), key = readKey(op, args);
  const following = useMemo(() => new Following(client, op, args), [client, op, key]); // eslint-disable-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  const snapshot = useSyncExternalStore(following.subscribe, following.getSnapshot, following.getSnapshot);
  return { ...snapshot, loadMore: following.loadMore, retry: following.retry, refresh: following.refresh };
}

/** A write. `run` never throws; `last` is the most recent outcome, including
 * queued settlement. A sent replay has `replayed: true` and no result. */
export interface MutationHook<A, Outcome> {
  run(args: A): Promise<Outcome>;
  last: Outcome | undefined;
  inFlight: boolean;
}
/** A durable write's hook: `run` waits for sent/failed independently of read
 * subscriptions and component lifetime. Offline it waits for reconnect.
 * Explicit `{ waitSeconds: 0 }` returns at custody; `{ id }` reuses saved intent. */
export interface WriteHook<A, R> {
  run(args: A, options?: MutateOptions): Promise<Write<R>>;
  /** Undefined before the first run. `isFailed(last)` narrows to the refusal
   * (`last.why`); `sentResult(last)` is the fresh result, if any (a replayed
   * receipt has none). */
  last: Write<R> | undefined;
  inFlight: boolean;
}
/** What `useMutation(op)` returns, named by the operation, for props:
 * `function Row({ remove }: { remove: UseMutation<typeof api.remove> })`. */
export type UseMutation<O> = O extends Ephemeral<infer A, infer R> ? MutationHook<A, Signal<R>>
  : O extends Mutation<infer A, infer R> ? WriteHook<A, R> : never;

function useTrackedMutation<A, R>(op: Mutation<A, R> | Ephemeral<A, R>, id?: string): MutationHook<A, Write<R> | Signal<R>> & { restoring?: boolean } {
  const client = useClient();
  const [last, setLast] = useState<Write<R> | Signal<R> | undefined>(undefined);
  const [inFlight, setInFlight] = useState(false);
  const restoration = useMemo(() => ({ pending: !!id }), [client, op, id]);
  const [, refreshRestoration] = useState(0);
  const lifetime = useRef({ active: true, pending: 0, next: 0, latest: 0, ids: new Map<string, number>(), early: new Map<string, Exclude<Write, { state: "pending" }>>() });
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!lifetime.current.active) {
      lifetime.current = { active: true, pending: 0, next: 0, latest: 0, ids: new Map(), early: new Map() };
      setLast(undefined);
      setInFlight(false);
    }
    const owner = lifetime.current;
    const restoredLookup = () => {
      if (owner.active && lifetime.current === owner && restoration.pending) {
        restoration.pending = false;
        refreshRestoration(n => n + 1);
      }
    };
    if (id) owner.ids.set(id, owner.latest);
    let restored = false;
    const unsubscribe = op.ephemeral ? () => {} : client.onWrite((write) => {
      const run = owner.ids.get(write.id);
      if (run == null) {
        // Settlement can win the same turn in which mutate returns pending.
        // Keep that terminal result until the returned id binds it to a run.
        if (owner.pending > 0) {
          owner.early.set(write.id, write);
          if (owner.early.size > 256) owner.early.delete(owner.early.keys().next().value!);
        }
        return;
      }
      owner.ids.delete(write.id);
      if (write.id === id) { restored = true; restoredLookup(); }
      if (owner.active && lifetime.current === owner && run === owner.latest) setLast(write as Write<R>);
    });
    if (id) void client.write(id).then(write => {
      if (!restored && owner.active && lifetime.current === owner && owner.latest === 0) {
        setLast(write as Write<R> | undefined);
      }
    }).catch(() => { /* No receipt is not a failed mutation. Keep the subscribed outcome. */ }).finally(restoredLookup);
    return () => { owner.active = false; unsubscribe(); };
  }, [client, op, id, restoration]);
  const run = useCallback(async (args: A, options?: MutateOptions): Promise<Write<R> | Signal<R>> => {
    const owner = lifetime.current;
    const serial = ++owner.next;
    owner.latest = serial;
    owner.pending++;
    if (owner.active) setInFlight(true);
    let outcome: Write<R> | Signal<R>;
    try { outcome = op.ephemeral ? await client.mutate(op, args) : await settleMutation(client, op, args, options); }
    catch (error) {
      // A foreign Client can throw without exposing its minted id. Do not
      // invent an operation identity or claim that this is safe to retry.
      outcome = { state: "failed", id: "", why: { code: "E_CLIENT", family: "client", message: `The client did not return a write outcome; whether it was admitted is unknown. ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}` } };
    }

import { pendingRead, readyRead } from "./read-existence.ts";
import type { Client, Query, Read, Observed, ObserveOptions, Cursor } from "./contract.ts";
import { isReady } from "./contract.ts";
import { peekObservation } from "./observe-watch.ts";
const LOADING: Read<never> = { loading: true };

/** The requested page chain, with one newest observed image per row ID. */
export class Pages<A extends { c?: Cursor | null }, R extends readonly unknown[]> {
  private pages: { cursor: Cursor | null; observed: Observed<R>; unsubscribe: () => void }[] = [];
  private requested = 1;
  private subs = new Set<() => void>();
  private cache: { items: R[number][]; hasMore: boolean; read: Read<R> } | null = null;
  private peeked: Read<R> | undefined;
  private cacheReads: Read<R>[] = [];
  private reconciling = false;
  private imageRevision = 0;
  private imageRevisions = new WeakMap<object, number>();
  private noteImage(read: Read<R>) {
    // Revalidation/freshness changes retain the same data array; they do not
    // make an older row image newer than an image delivered on another page.
    if (isReady(read) && Array.isArray(read.data) && !this.imageRevisions.has(read.data))
      this.imageRevisions.set(read.data, ++this.imageRevision);
    return read;
  }
  constructor(private client: Client, private op: Query<A, R>, private args: A, private options?: ObserveOptions) {}
  private open(c: Cursor | null) {
    const observed = this.client.observe(this.op, { ...this.args, c }, this.options);
    const page = { cursor: c, observed, unsubscribe: () => {} };
    this.pages.push(page);
    page.unsubscribe = observed.subscribe(() => {
      if (this.pages.includes(page)) this.notify();
    });
  }
  private drop(from: number) {
    for (const page of this.pages.splice(from)) {
      page.unsubscribe();
      page.observed.close();
    }
  }
  private notify() {
    if (this.reconciling) return;
    this.reconciling = true;
    try {
      // A later page belongs to its predecessor's current cursor. Keep the
      // requested depth, but discard the old suffix before opening a new one:
      // deduplication alone cannot recover rows an old boundary skipped.
      for (let i = 0; i < this.pages.length; i++) {
        const read = this.noteImage(this.pages[i]!.observed.getSnapshot());
        const next = isReady(read) && Array.isArray(read.data) ? read.next : null;
        if (!next || i + 1 >= this.requested || this.pages.slice(0, i + 1).some((p) => p.cursor === next)) {
          this.drop(i + 1);
          break;
        }
        if (this.pages[i + 1]?.cursor !== next) {
          this.drop(i + 1);
          this.open(next);
        }
      }
      this.cache = null;
    } finally { this.reconciling = false; }
    for (const s of this.subs) s();
  }
  subscribe = (notify: () => void) => {
    this.subs.add(notify);
    if (!this.pages.length) { this.open(null); this.notify(); }
    let active = true;
    return () => {
      if (!active) return;
      active = false;
      this.subs.delete(notify);
      if (!this.subs.size) { this.drop(0); this.cache = null; }
    };
  };
  getSnapshot = () => {
    const peeked = this.pages.length ? undefined : peekObservation(this.client, this.op, { ...this.args, c: null }, this.options);
    // An unsubscribed render owns no notifications: recheck the live snapshot
    // and the linger cutoff on every call, caching only its derived page shape.
    if (peeked !== this.peeked) { this.peeked = peeked; this.cache = null; }
    // @ref LLP 3000.023#5 — page accessors check deadlines before a combined cache can escape.
    let sources, reads: Read<R>[];
    do {
      sources = [...this.pages];
      reads = sources.length ? sources.map(page => this.noteImage(page.observed.getSnapshot())) : peeked ? [this.noteImage(peeked)] : [];
      // A deadline check may synchronously drop a suffix through notify().
    } while (sources.length !== this.pages.length || sources.some((page, i) => page !== this.pages[i]));
    if (reads.length !== this.cacheReads.length || reads.some((read, i) => read !== this.cacheReads[i])) this.cache = null;
    this.cacheReads = reads;
    if (this.cache) return this.cache;
    const items: R[number][] = [];
    const identities = new Map<string, { index: number; revision: number }>();
    let last: Read<R> = LOADING as Read<R>;
    let complete = true, fresh = true, revalidating = false, pending = false;
    let cut: import("./contract.ts").ReadCut = null;
    let since: number | undefined;
    let knownSince = true;
    let loadingMore = false;
    for (const read of reads) {
      // @ref LLP 3000.019#3.3 — a pending next page keeps the ready prefix on screen.
      // Resets of the first page and refusals still replace the combined read.
      if ("loading" in read && isReady(last)) { loadingMore = true; break; }
      last = read;
      if (!isReady(read)) break;
      if (!Array.isArray(read.data)) { last = LOADING as Read<R>; break; }
      // @ref LLP 3000.028#3.3 — keyset edits may repeat IDs across pages.
      // Keep the first display position and the most recently observed image,
      // including a refreshed earlier page. Only compiler-proved source row IDs are accumulation keys; arbitrary
      // projections preserve ordinary list semantics, including a field named id.
      const revision = this.imageRevisions.get(read.data)!;
      for (const item of read.data as readonly R[number][]) {
        const id = this.op.rowKey === "id" && item && typeof item === "object" && "id" in item ? item.id : undefined;
        const previous = typeof id === "string" ? identities.get(id) : undefined;
        if (previous) {
          if (revision >= previous.revision) {
            items[previous.index] = item;
            previous.revision = revision;
          }
        } else {
          if (typeof id === "string") identities.set(id, { index: items.length, revision });
          items.push(item);
        }
      }
      pending ||= pendingRead(read);
      complete &&= read.complete;
      if (read.cut === "meter" || (cut === null && read.cut === "words")) cut = read.cut;
      fresh &&= read.fresh;
      revalidating ||= read.revalidating === true;
      if (!read.fresh) {
        if (read.since == null) knownSince = false;
        else since = Math.min(since ?? read.since, read.since);
      }
    }
    const hasMore = !loadingMore && isReady(last) && last.next != null && !this.pages.some((p) => p.cursor === last.next);
    const read: Read<R> = isReady(last)
      ? readyRead({ data: items as unknown as R, complete, cut, fresh, ...(revalidating ? { revalidating: true } : {}), ...(knownSince && since != null ? { since } : {}), next: last.next ?? null }, pending || loadingMore)
      : last;
    this.cache = { items, hasMore, read };
    return this.cache;
  };
  loadMore = () => {
    if (!this.subs.size || !this.getSnapshot().hasMore) return;
    this.requested = Math.max(this.requested, this.pages.length + 1);
    this.notify();
  };
}

+## List read state
+
+`ReadState` from snapback4/react renders a list read or `usePage` result in one
+expression. Loading/empty default to null; omitted denied throws QueryRefusal.
+Empty describes returned rows, including partial/stale lists, not proven absence.
+The data renderer receives the same precise read metadata. Supply Text/View
+slots in React Native; the component creates no observation or retained state.
+
+```tsx
+import { ReadState, type Read } from "snapback4/react";
+export function ListScreen({ read }: { read: Read<readonly { id: string; title: string }[]> }) {
+  return <ReadState read={read} loading={<p>Loading…</p>} empty={<p>No results</p>} denied={why => <p role="alert">{why.message}</p>}>{(rows, answer) => <ul data-complete={answer.complete}>{rows.map(row => <li key={row.id}>{row.title}</li>)}</ul>}</ReadState>;
+}
+```

### 3.4 P8: residency you can see, and a CLI that does not fight the dev server

**Change.**

- `client.residency()` returns rows and bytes per table on the device, with
  the store's total bytes and, on the web, the wasm heap. The guide's residency
  card shows it next to the sync windows that bound it.
- `snapback4 run <job>` and the other store-writing CLI commands detect a live
  dev server on the same store (its lifetime lock file) and either run the work
  through that server or refuse with `E_STORE_BUSY`, naming the server's
  address, instead of failing with `database is locked`. Which of the two is
  the lane's first finding.

**Evidence.** Residency on a fixture with known rows; the CLI against a running
dev server, both ways.

**2026-10-08 — `run` goes through a live dev host (app-farm round 1).** The
lane's first finding was the refusal; 27 of ~270 app-farm builds (41 diaries)
then stopped their dev server to run one operation, or reverse-engineered the
wire. `run` now takes the other branch of this item when the owner is a
responsive `snapback4 dev` (it answers `GET /dev/status`): a query or mutation
goes to `POST /q|/m/<op>` with the persona header naming the same principal a
local run would use, and a job to the dev-only `POST /dev/jobs/<job>`, which
queues it behind earlier runs and drives chunks on the dev clock. No second
writer opens the store. `--now`, a non-persona principal, `serve` and a stopped
host still refuse `E_STORE_BUSY`, now with the equivalent `curl`. Other
store-writing commands keep the refusal.

**2026-09-27 — Darwin ownership correction (lane OW).** Ownership now locks
`<database filename>-owner` beside the canonical database, a regular 0600 file
opened with `O_NOFOLLOW`: exclusive for backend writers, shared for devices
including the native C ABI. On macOS/iOS, a flock on the database itself
conflicts with SQLite's POSIX locks, preventing startup adoption and device
commits. Database identity remains `(dev, ino)`, checked with stat alone;
only a missing database is created and closed before SQLite opens it. The
guard holds the sidecar, never a database descriptor whose close could discard
SQLite's locks. Sidecars persist after unlock and move with the database's
other sidecars; symlinks, hard links and nonregular ownership files are refused.
`serve.lock` remains an address hint, and `E_STORE_BUSY` keeps its meaning.

**2026-09-27 — round-1 file-mutation hardening (lane OW).** Both ownership
and address-file opens lstat the database and candidate before opening and
compare the opened inode again before any lock, read, write or chmod. A
post-open alias or uncertain descriptor is deliberately forgotten, never
closed or unlocked: either operation could discard SQLite's POSIX locks.
Ownership sidecars must be empty, and address records at most 128 bytes;
these stat-only bounds also refuse a SQLite database renamed to either name
when its original path is absent. Lock the sidecar before creating a missing

/// The starter README for a screen: the Todos README describes the starter's
/// own schema and screen; beside a project's schema (the neutral `Home`) the
/// README is named after the directory and describes that schema's sign-in.
// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000#7.4 — wave 6 (042): an adapted starter kept a README about todos and guest sign-in.
pub(super) fn readme(platform: Platform, title: &str, body: &Body, personas: bool, offline: &Offline) -> String {
    let todos = match platform { Platform::Web => include_str!("starter/web/README.md"), Platform::Expo => include_str!("starter/expo/README.md") };
    if *body == Body::Todos {
        return todos.replace("native device and work offline;", "native device;")
            .replace("wasm device.\n", &format!("wasm device.\n\n{}\n", offline.paragraph(platform)));
    }
    let home = match platform { Platform::Web => include_str!("starter/web/README.home.md"), Platform::Expo => include_str!("starter/expo/README.home.md") };
    let text = home.replacen("# TITLE", &format!("# {title}"), 1).replace("SIGN_IN", if personas { PERSONA_SIGN_IN } else { GUEST_SIGN_IN })
        .replacen("OFFLINE\n", &format!("{}\n", offline.paragraph(platform)), 1);
    if platform == Platform::Web { return text; }
    // The Expo toolchain notes are the Todos README's own, word for word.
    let advisories = todos.split_once("\n> ").map(|(_, rest)| format!("> {}", rest.split_once("\n\n").expect("the advisory box ends").0)).expect("the Expo README has its advisory box");
    let toolchain = todos.split_once("\nKeep the Expo and").map(|(_, rest)| format!("Keep the Expo and{}", rest.split_once("## Next steps").expect("the Expo README has next steps").0)).expect("the Expo README has its toolchain notes");
    text.replacen("ADVISORIES", &advisories, 1).replacen("TOOLCHAIN\n", &toolchain, 1)
}

/// The Expo app's `app.json` ids, named after the directory's title: a slug
/// (`bake-sale`), a URL scheme and a bundle id that start with a letter
/// (`bakesale`, `dev.snapback4.bakesale`).
pub(super) fn app_ids(title: &str) -> (String, String, String) {
    let words: Vec<String> = title.split(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_alphanumeric()).filter(|word| !word.is_empty()).map(str::to_ascii_lowercase).collect();
    let slug = if words.is_empty() { "app".to_owned() } else { words.join("-") };
    let mut scheme = words.concat();
    if !scheme.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_alphabetic()) { scheme = format!("app{scheme}"); }
    let bundle = format!("dev.snapback4.{scheme}");
    (slug, scheme, bundle)
}

/// Which starter screen pair: the guest sign-in, or the persona picker.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub(super) enum Platform { Web, Expo }

impl Platform {
    /// Where the starter writes its screen and its client.
    pub(super) fn paths(self) -> (&'static str, &'static str) {
        match self { Platform::Web => ("src/App.tsx", "src/client.ts"), Platform::Expo => ("App.tsx", "src/client.ts") }
    }
}

/// The screen a signed-in viewer sees: the starter's `Todos`, which calls
/// list/add/toggle/remove, or `Home`, which compiles against any schema (the
/// viewer and the generated api's operation names, for the project to replace),
/// with one real read when the schema has a query that takes no required
/// arguments (its `api` path, `notes` or `module.notes`).
// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000#7.4 — a starter screen must typecheck against the schema beside it.
// @ref LLP 3000.013#6.6 — wave 5: the adapted Home renders one useQuery through matchRead, the idioms Todos taught.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub(super) enum Body { Todos, Home(Option<String>) }

/// The starter's screen and client for a schema: the guest sign-in, or, with
/// `personas`, the persona picker, around `body`. The texts are as the
/// starter ships them, before init's port rewrite.
fn screens_version(platform: Platform, personas: Option<&[String]>, body: &Body, previous: bool) -> (String, String) {
    let version = |current, old| if previous { old } else { current };
    let (guest, guest_client, persona, persona_client, todos, home) = match platform {
        Platform::Web => (include_str!("starter/web/guest.tsx"), version(include_str!("starter/web/client.ts"), include_str!("starter/previous/wave9/web-client.ts")), include_str!("starter/personas/web-app.tsx"), include_str!("starter/personas/web-client.ts"), version(include_str!("starter/web/todos.tsx"), include_str!("starter/previous/wave9/web-todos.tsx")), include_str!("starter/web/home.tsx")),
        Platform::Expo => (include_str!("starter/expo/guest.tsx"), version(include_str!("starter/expo/client.ts"), include_str!("starter/previous/wave9/expo-client.ts")), version(include_str!("starter/personas/expo-app.tsx"), include_str!("starter/previous/wave9/expo-personas.tsx")), include_str!("starter/personas/expo-client.ts"), version(include_str!("starter/expo/todos.tsx"), include_str!("starter/previous/wave9/expo-todos.tsx")), include_str!("starter/expo/home.tsx")),
    };
    let first_read = match platform { Platform::Web => include_str!("starter/web/first-read.tsx"), Platform::Expo => include_str!("starter/expo/first-read.tsx") };
    let (head, client) = match personas {
        None => (guest, guest_client.to_owned()),
        Some(personas) => {
            let list = personas.iter().map(|name| serde_json::to_string(name).unwrap()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
            (persona, persona_client.replace("PERSONAS", &format!("[{list}]")))
        }
    };
    let app = match body {
        Body::Todos => compose(head, todos),
        Body::Home(op) => {
            let (head, home) = if personas.is_some() { (persona_head_home(head), persona_home(home)) } else { (head.replace("<Todos />", "<Home />"), home.to_owned()) };
            match op {
                None => compose(&head, &home.replace("    <FirstRead />\n", "")),
                Some(op) => compose(&compose(&head, &home), &first_read.replace("api.OP", &format!("api.{op}"))),
            }
        }
    };
    (super::without_design_references(&app), super::without_design_references(&client))
}
